1.3.m: Gandharva singers, Kinnaras, and the hosts of apsarases / danced, sang, and praised, along with the Siddhas, Cāraṇas, and Guhyakas.

1.3.s:
evaṃ vijayamāpannaḥ śakro devesvarastadā..
devairhatāstadā daityāḥ patitāste mahītale.. 14.25 ..
1.3.d:
एवं विजयमापन्नः शक्रो देवेस्वरस्तदा..
देवैर्हतास्तदा दैत्याः पतितास्ते महीतले.. 14.25 ..
1.3.m: Having thus attained victory, Śakra, the lord of gods, / [surveyed] the Daityas who had been slain by the gods and lay fallen upon the earth.

1.3.s:
gatāsavo mahātmāno balipramukhato hyamī..
tapastaptuṃ purā vipro bhārgavo mānasottaram.. 14.26 ..
1.3.d:
गतासवो महात्मानो बलिप्रमुखतो ह्यमी..
तपस्तप्तुं पुरा विप्रो भार्गवो मानसोत्तरम्.. 14.26 ..
1.3.m: Lifeless were those great-souled ones headed by Bali. / Formerly, the brāhmaṇa Bhārgava had gone to Mount Mānasottara to perform austerity

1.3.s:
gataḥ śiṣyaiḥ parivṛtastasmādyuddhaṃ na veda tat..
avaśeṣāśca ye daityāste gatā bhārgavaṃ prati .. 14.27 ..
1.3.d:
गतः शिष्यैः परिवृतस्तस्माद्युद्धं न वेद तत्..
अवशेषाश्च ये दैत्यास्ते गता भार्गवं प्रति .. 14.27 ..
1.3.m: surrounded by his disciples; therefore he knew nothing of that war. / The remaining Daityas went to Bhārgava.

1.3.s:
kathitaṃ vai mahaddhṛttamasurāṇāṃ kṣayāvaham..
niśamya manyumāviṣṭo hyāgato bhṛgunaṃdanaḥ.. 14.28 ..
1.3.d:
कथितं वै महद्धृत्तमसुराणां क्षयावहम्..
निशम्य मन्युमाविष्टो ह्यागतो भृगुनंदनः.. 14.28 ..
1.3.m: The great disaster that brought about the destruction of the Asuras was related to him. / Hearing it, the son of Bhṛgu was overcome with wrath and came there.

1.3.s:
śiṣyaiḥ parivṛto bhūtvā mṛtāṃstānasurānapi..
vidyayā mṛtajīvinyā patitānsamajīvayat.. 14.29 ..
1.3.d:
शिष्यैः परिवृतो भूत्वा मृतांस्तानसुरानपि..
विद्यया मृतजीविन्या पतितान्समजीवयत्.. 14.29 ..
1.3.m: Surrounded by his disciples, he restored those slain and fallen Asuras to life / by means of the Mṛtasaṃjīvanī lore.

1.3.s:
nidrāpāyagatā yadvadutthitāste tadā'surāḥ..
utthitaḥ sa baliḥ prāha bhārgavaṃ hyamitadyutim.. 14.30 ..
1.3.d:
निद्रापायगता यद्वदुत्थितास्ते तदाऽसुराः..
उत्थितः स बलिः प्राह भार्गवं ह्यमितद्युतिम्.. 14.30 ..
1.3.m: Like men awakened from sleep, the Asuras then arose. / Arising, Bali spoke to Bhārgava of immeasurable splendor:

1.3.s:
jīvitena kimadyaiva mama nāsti prayojanam..
pātitastridaśeṃdreṇa yathā kāpuruṣastathā.. 14.31 ..
1.3.d:
जीवितेन किमद्यैव मम नास्ति प्रयोजनम्..
पातितस्त्रिदशेंद्रेण यथा कापुरुषस्तथा.. 14.31 ..
1.3.m: “What use do I have for life today? I have none, / having been struck down by the lord of the thirty [gods] like a coward!”

1.3.s:
balinoktaṃ vacaḥ śrutvā śukro vacanamabravīt..
manasvino hi ye śūrāḥ pataṃti samare budhā.. 14.32 ..
1.3.d:
बलिनोक्तं वचः श्रुत्वा शुक्रो वचनमब्रवीत्..
मनस्विनो हि ये शूराः पतंति समरे बुधा.. 14.32 ..
1.3.m: Hearing the words spoken by Bali, Śukra said: / “The resolute heroes and wise men who fall in battle,

1.3.s:
ye śastreṇa hatāḥ sadyo mriyamāṇā vrajaṃti vai..
triviṣṭapaṃ na saṃdeha iti vedānuśāsanam.. 14.33 ..
1.3.d:
ये शस्त्रेण हताः सद्यो म्रियमाणा व्रजंति वै..
त्रिविष्टपं न संदेह इति वेदानुशासनम्.. 14.33 ..
1.3.m: and die slain by a weapon, go directly / to heaven; of this there is no doubt—such is the ordinance of the Veda.”

1.3.s:
evamāśvāsayāmāsa balinaṃ bhṛgunaṃdanaḥ..
tapastatāpa vividhaṃ daityānāṃ siddhidāyakam.. 14.34 ..
1.3.d:
एवमाश्वासयामास बलिनं भृगुनंदनः..
तपस्तताप विविधं दैत्यानां सिद्धिदायकम्.. 14.34 ..
1.3.m: Thus the son of Bhṛgu consoled Bali, / and performed diverse austerities that bestow success upon the Daityas.

1.3.s:
tathā daitya gatāḥ sarve bhṛguṇā ca pracoditāḥ..
pātālamavasansarve balimukhyāḥ sukhena vai.. 14.35 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe devāsurasaṃgrāme bhārgaveṇa mṛtadaityasaṃjīvanavarṇanaṃnāma caturdaśo'dhyāyaḥ.. 14 .. cha ..
1.3.d:
तथा दैत्य गताः सर्वे भृगुणा च प्रचोदिताः..
पातालमवसन्सर्वे बलिमुख्याः सुखेन वै.. 14.35 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे देवासुरसंग्रामे भार्गवेण मृतदैत्यसंजीवनवर्णनंनाम चतुर्दशोऽध्यायः.. 14 .. छ ..
1.3.m:
Then all the Daityas, impelled by Bhṛgu, / went to Pātāla, and all of them, headed by Bali, dwelt there happily.
Thus ends the fourteenth chapter, titled “The Description of the Reviving of the Slain Daityas by Bhārgava during the Battle between the Gods and Asuras,” in the First Section, the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, of the Skandapurāṇa comprising eighty-one thousand verses.

1.3.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ..
rājyaṃ prāpto hi deveṃdraḥ kathitaste guruṃ vinā..
guroravajñayā jāto rājyabhraṃśo hi tasya tu.. 15.1 ..
1.3.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः..
राज्यं प्राप्तो हि देवेंद्रः कथितस्ते गुरुं विना..
गुरोरवज्ञया जातो राज्यभ्रंशो हि तस्य तु.. 15.1 ..
1.3.m: The ṛṣis said: / You have told us that the lord of the gods obtained the kingdom without his guru; / yet his fall from kingship occurred through disrespect toward his guru.

1.3.s:
kena praṇoditaśceṃdro babhūva ciramāsane..
tatsarvaṃ kathayāśu tvaṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi naḥ.. 15.2 ..
1.3.d:
केन प्रणोदितश्चेंद्रो बभूव चिरमासने..
तत्सर्वं कथयाशु त्वं परं कौतूहलं हि नः.. 15.2 ..
1.3.m: Impelled by whom did Indra sit on his throne for a long time? / Tell us all that quickly, for great is our curiosity.

1.3.s:
..lomaśa uvāca..
guruṇāpi vinā rājyaṃ kṛtavānsa śacīpatiḥ..
viśvarūpoktavidhinā iṃdro rājye sthito mahān.. 15.3 ..
1.3.d:
..लोमश उवाच..
गुरुणापि विना राज्यं कृतवान्स शचीपतिः..
विश्वरूपोक्तविधिना इंद्रो राज्ये स्थितो महान्.. 15.3 ..
1.3.m: Lomaśa said: / Even without his guru, that husband of Śacī ruled his kingdom; / by the procedure proclaimed by Viśvarūpa, great Indra remained in his rule.

1.3.s:
viśvakarmasuto viprā viśvarūpo mahānṛpaḥ..
purohito'tha śakrasya yājakaścābhavattadā.. 15.4 ..
1.3.d:
विश्वकर्मसुतो विप्रा विश्वरूपो महानृपः..
पुरोहितोऽथ शक्रस्य याजकश्चाभवत्तदा.. 15.4 ..
1.3.m: O brahmins, the son of Viśvakarman was Viśvarūpa, a great king; / he then became the domestic priest and the sacrificing priest of Śakra.

1.3.s:
tasminyajñe'vadānaiśca yajane asurānsurān..
manuṣyāṃścaiva triśirā aparokṣaṃ śacīpateḥ.. 15.5 ..
1.3.d:
तस्मिन्यज्ञेऽवदानैश्च यजने असुरान्सुरान्..
मनुष्यांश्चैव त्रिशिरा अपरोक्षं शचीपतेः.. 15.5 ..
1.3.m: In that sacrifice, with oblations and rites, the three-headed one [offered] to the Asuras, gods, / and men, out of the sight of Śacī's husband.

1.3.s:
devāndadāti sākrośaṃ daityāṃstūṣṇīmathādadāt..
manuṣyānmadhyapātena pratyahaṃ sa grahāndvijaḥ.. 15.6 ..
1.3.d:
देवान्ददाति साक्रोशं दैत्यांस्तूष्णीमथाददात्..
मनुष्यान्मध्यपातेन प्रत्यहं स ग्रहान्द्विजः.. 15.6 ..
1.3.m: He gave to the gods with loud declaration, but he offered to the Daityas silently; / to men he gave with an impartial portion; thus did that twice-born offer the libations every day.

1.3.s:
ekadā tu maheṃdreṇa sūcito gurulāghavāt..
alakṣyamāṇena tadā jñātaṃ tasya cikīrṣitam.. 15.7 ..
1.3.d:
एकदा तु महेंद्रेण सूचितो गुरुलाघवात्..
अलक्ष्यमाणेन तदा ज्ञातं तस्य चिकीर्षितम्.. 15.7 ..
1.3.m: Once, however, prompted by Mahendra due to the lightness [of his regard] for his guru, / his design was perceived though he was unobserved:

1.3.s:
daityānāṃ kāryasiddhyarthamavadānaṃ prayacchati..
asau purohito'smākaṃ pareṣāṃ ca phalapradaḥ.. 15.8 ..
1.3.d:
दैत्यानां कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थमवदानं प्रयच्छति..
असौ पुरोहितोऽस्माकं परेषां च फलप्रदः.. 15.8 ..
1.3.m: “For the accomplishment of the Daityas’ ends he offers the oblation; / this priest of ours grants the fruit to our enemies!”

1.3.s:
iti matvā tadā śakro vajreṇa śataparvaṇā..
ciccheda tacchirāṃsyeva tatkṣaṇādabhavadvadhaḥ.. 15.9 ..
1.3.d:
इति मत्वा तदा शक्रो वज्रेण शतपर्वणा..
चिच्छेद तच्छिरांस्येव तत्क्षणादभवद्वधः.. 15.9 ..
1.3.m: Thinking thus, Śakra then severed his heads / with his hundred-jointed vajra; in that instant his death occurred.

1.3.s:
yenākarotsomapānamajāyaṃta kapiṃjalāḥ..
tatonyena surāpānātkalaviṃkā bhavanmukhāt.. 15.10 ..
1.3.d:
येनाकरोत्सोमपानमजायंत कपिंजलाः..
ततोन्येन सुरापानात्कलविंका भवन्मुखात्.. 15.10 ..
1.3.m: From the head with which he drank Soma, kapiñjala birds were born; / from the other, from drinking liquor, sparrows arose from the mouth;

1.3.s:
anyānanādajāyaṃta tittirā viśvarūpiṇaḥ..
evaṃ hato viśvarūpaḥ śakreṇa maṃdabhāginā.. 15.11 ..
1.3.d:
अन्याननादजायंत तित्तिरा विश्वरूपिणः..
एवं हतो विश्वरूपः शक्रेण मंदभागिना.. 15.11 ..
1.3.m: from the other mouth were born the partridges of diverse forms. / Thus was Viśvarūpa slain by unfortunate Śakra.

1.3.s:
brahmahatyā tadodbhūtā durdharṣā ca bhayāvahā..
durdharṣā durmukhā duṣṭā caṇḍālarajasānvitā.. 15.12 ..
1.3.d:
ब्रह्महत्या तदोद्भूता दुर्धर्षा च भयावहा..
दुर्धर्षा दुर्मुखा दुष्टा चण्डालरजसान्विता.. 15.12 ..
1.3.m: Then arose [the sin of] brahmin-slaughter, irresistible and terrifying, / unassailable, hideous-faced, wicked, and smeared with the menstrual blood of an outcaste.

1.3.s:
brahmahatyā surāpānaṃ steyaṃ gurvaṃganāgamaḥ..
ityeṣāmapyaghavatāmidameva ca niṣkṛtiḥ.. 15.13 ..
1.3.d:
ब्रह्महत्या सुरापानं स्तेयं गुर्वंगनागमः..
इत्येषामप्यघवतामिदमेव च निष्कृतिः.. 15.13 ..
1.3.m: Slaying a brahmin, drinking liquor, theft, and union with the guru's wife— / even for those who commit these sins, this alone is the expiation:

1.3.s:
nāmavyāharaṇaṃ viṣṇoryatastadviṣayā matiḥ..
triśirā dhūmrahastā sā śakraṃ grastumupāyayau.. 15.14 ..
1.3.d:
नामव्याहरणं विष्णोर्यतस्तद्विषया मतिः..
त्रिशिरा धूम्रहस्ता सा शक्रं ग्रस्तुमुपाययौ.. 15.14 ..
1.3.m: the uttering of Viṣṇu’s name, for the mind becomes fixed on him. / Having three heads and smoke-colored hands, she approached to swallow Śakra.

1.3.s:
tato bhayena mahatā palāyanaparo'bhavat..
palāyamānaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā hyanuyātā bhayāvahā.. 15.15 ..
1.3.d:
ततो भयेन महता पलायनपरोऽभवत्..
पलायमानं तं दृष्ट्वा ह्यनुयाता भयावहा.. 15.15 ..
1.3.m: Then, out of great fear, he took to flight. / Seeing him fleeing, that terrifying woman pursued him.

1.3.s:
yato dhāvati sā'dhāvattiṣṭhaṃtamanutiṣṭhati..
aṃgakṛtā yathā chāyā śakrasyapariveṣṭitum..
āyāti tāvatsahasā iṃdro'pyapsu nyamajjata.. 15.16 ..
1.3.d:
यतो धावति साऽधावत्तिष्ठंतमनुतिष्ठति..
अंगकृता यथा छाया शक्रस्यपरिवेष्टितुम्..
आयाति तावत्सहसा इंद्रोऽप्यप्सु न्यमज्जत.. 15.16 ..
1.3.m: Wherever he ran, she ran; wherever he stood, she stood close behind him, / like a shadow clinging to a body. As she came hastily to encompass Śakra, / Indra plunged into the waters,

1.3.s: śīghratvena yathā viprāściraṃtanajalecaraḥ.. 15.17 ..
1.3.d: शीघ्रत्वेन यथा विप्राश्चिरंतनजलेचरः.. 15.17 ..
1.3.m: as swiftly, O brahmins, as an ancient aquatic creature.

1.3.s:
evaṃ divyaśataṃ pūrṇaṃ varṣāṇāṃ ca śacīpateḥ..
vasatastasya duḥkhena tathā caiva śatadvayam..
arājakaṃ tadā jātaṃ nākapṛṣṭhe bhayāvaham.. 15.18 ..
1.3.d:
एवं दिव्यशतं पूर्णं वर्षाणां च शचीपतेः..
वसतस्तस्य दुःखेन तथा चैव शतद्वयम्..
अराजकं तदा जातं नाकपृष्ठे भयावहम्.. 15.18 ..
1.3.m: In this way, as Śacī’s husband dwelt in sorrow / for a full one hundred divine years, and likewise two hundred, / the surface of heaven then became kingless and terrifying.

1.3.s:
tadā ciṃtānvitā devā ṛṣayo'pi tapasvinaḥ..
trailokyaṃ cā''padā grastaṃ babhūva ca tadā dvijāḥ.. 15.19 ..
1.3.d:
तदा चिंतान्विता देवा ऋषयोऽपि तपस्विनः..
त्रैलोक्यं चा'ऽपदा ग्रस्तं बभूव च तदा द्विजाः.. 15.19 ..
1.3.m: Then the gods and ascetic ṛṣis were filled with anxiety, / and the three worlds were seized by misfortune, O twice-born.

1.3.s:
eko'pi brahmahā yatra rāṣṭre vasati nirbhayaḥ..
akālamaraṇaṃ tatra sādhūnāmupajāyate.. 15.20 ..
1.3.d:
एकोऽपि ब्रह्महा यत्र राष्ट्रे वसति निर्भयः..
अकालमरणं तत्र साधूनामुपजायते.. 15.20 ..
1.3.m: In whatever realm even a single slayer of a brahmin dwells without fear, / untimely death befalls the virtuous there.

1.3.s:
rājā pāpayuto yasminrāṣṭre vasati tatra vai..
durbhikṣaṃ caiva maraṇaṃ tathaivopadravā dvijāḥ.. 15.21 ..
1.3.d:
राजा पापयुतो यस्मिन्राष्ट्रे वसति तत्र वै..
दुर्भिक्षं चैव मरणं तथैवोपद्रवा द्विजाः.. 15.21 ..
1.3.m: In whatever realm a sinful king dwells, / famine, death, and afflictions occur there, O twice-born.

1.3.s:
bhavaṃti bahavo'narthāḥ prajānāṃ nāśahetave..
tasmādrājñā tu kartavyo dharmmaḥ śraddhāpareṇa hi.. 15.22 ..
1.3.d:
भवंति बहवोऽनर्थाः प्रजानां नाशहेतवे..
तस्माद्राज्ञा तु कर्तव्यो धर्म्मः श्रद्धापरेण हि.. 15.22 ..
1.3.m: Many calamities occur bringing destruction to the subjects; / therefore, a king must surely perform dharma with supreme faith.

1.3.s:
tathā prakṛtayo rājñaḥ śucajitvena pratiṣṭhitāḥ..
indreṇa ca kṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tena pāpena vai dvijāḥ..
nānāvidhairmahātāpaiḥ sopadravamabhūjjagat.. 15.23 ..
1.3.d:
तथा प्रकृतयो राज्ञः शुचजित्वेन प्रतिष्ठिताः..
इन्द्रेण च कृतं पापं तेन पापेन वै द्विजाः..
नानाविधैर्महातापैः सोपद्रवमभूज्जगत्.. 15.23 ..
1.3.m: The king's subjects are established in accordance with his purity; / by the sin committed by Indra, O twice-born, / the world became plagued with diverse great afflictions.

1.3.s:
..śaunaka uvāca..
aśvamedhaśatenaiva prāptaṃ rājyaṃ mahattaram..
devānāmakhilaṃ sūta kasmādvighramajāyata..
śakrasya ca mahābhāga yathāvatkathayasva na.. 15.24 ..
1.3.d:
..शौनक उवाच..
अश्वमेधशतेनैव प्राप्तं राज्यं महत्तरम्..
देवानामखिलं सूत कस्माद्विघ्रमजायत..
शक्रस्य च महाभाग यथावत्कथयस्व न.. 15.24 ..
1.3.m: Śaunaka said: / By a hundred horse-sacrifices alone, the supreme sovereignty / over all the gods was attained; why, O Sūta, did an obstacle arise / for Śakra? Tell us properly, O highly fortunate one.

1.3.s:
..sūta uvāca..
devānāṃ dānavānāṃ ca manuṣyāṇāṃ viśeṣataḥ..
karmmaiva sukhaduḥkhānāṃ hetubhūtaṃ na saṃśayaḥ.. 15.25 ..
1.3.d:
..सूत उवाच..
देवानां दानवानां च मनुष्याणां विशेषतः..
कर्म्मैव सुखदुःखानां हेतुभूतं न संशयः.. 15.25 ..
1.3.m: Sūta said: / For gods, demons, and especially for men, / action alone is the cause of pleasures and pains, without doubt.

1.3.s:
indreṇa ca kṛtaṃ viprā mahadbhūtaṃ jugupsitam..
guroravajñā ca kṛtā viśvarūpavadhaḥ kṛtaḥ.. 15.26 ..
1.3.d:
इन्द्रेण च कृतं विप्रा महद्भूतं जुगुप्सितम्..
गुरोरवज्ञा च कृता विश्वरूपवधः कृतः.. 15.26 ..
1.3.m: A great, repulsive deed was committed by Indra, O brahmins: / disrespect was shown to the guru, and the slaying of Viśvarūpa was committed.

1.3.s:
gautamasya guroḥ patnī sevitā tasya tatphalam..
prāptaṃ maheṃdreṇa ciraṃ yasya nāsti pratikriyā.. 15.27 ..
1.3.d:
गौतमस्य गुरोः पत्नी सेविता तस्य तत्फलम्..
प्राप्तं महेंद्रेण चिरं यस्य नास्ति प्रतिक्रिया.. 15.27 ..
1.3.m: The wife of the guru Gautama was violated; / the fruit of that, for which there is no remedy, was obtained by Mahendra for a long time.

1.3.s:
ye hi dṛṣkaṭatakarmmāṇo na kurvaṃti ca niṣkṛtim..
durdaśāṃ prapnuvantyete yathaivendraḥ śatakratuḥ.. 15.28 ..
1.3.d:
ये हि दृष्कटतकर्म्माणो न कुर्वंति च निष्कृतिम्..
दुर्दशां प्रप्नुवन्त्येते यथैवेन्द्रः शतक्रतुः.. 15.28 ..
1.3.m: Those who commit evil deeds and perform no expiation / meet with a miserable plight, just like Indra, who performed a hundred sacrifices.

1.3.s:
duṣkṛtopārjitasyā taḥ prāyāścittaṃ hi tatkṣaṇāt..
kartavyaṃ vidhivadviprāḥ sarvapāpopaśāṃtaye.. 15.29 ..
1.3.d:
दुष्कृतोपार्जितस्या तः प्रायाश्चित्तं हि तत्क्षणात्..
कर्तव्यं विधिवद्विप्राः सर्वपापोपशांतये.. 15.29 ..
1.3.m: Therefore, an expiation for what has been acquired through an evil deed / must be performed instantly and according to the rules, O brahmins, for the appeasement of all sins.

1.3.s: upapātakamadhyastaṃ mahāpātakatāṃ vrajet.. 15.30 ..
1.3.d: उपपातकमध्यस्तं महापातकतां व्रजेत्.. 15.30 ..
1.3.m: [An unexpiated] minor sin becomes transformed into a major sin.

1.3.s:
tataḥ svadharmaniṣṭhāṃ ca ye kurvaṃti sadā narāḥ..
prātarmadhyāhnasāyāhne teṣāṃ pāpaṃ vinaśyati.. 15.31 ..
1.3.d:
ततः स्वधर्मनिष्ठां च ये कुर्वंति सदा नराः..
प्रातर्मध्याह्नसायाह्ने तेषां पापं विनश्यति.. 15.31 ..
1.3.m: Furthermore, the sin of those men who always abide in their own dharma / is destroyed in the morning, at noon, and in the evening.

1.3.s:
prāpnuvaṃtyuttamaṃ lokaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā..
tasmādasau durācāraḥ prāpte vai karmaṇaḥ phalam.. 15.32 ..
1.3.d:
प्राप्नुवंत्युत्तमं लोकं नात्र कार्या विचारणा..
तस्मादसौ दुराचारः प्राप्ते वै कर्मणः फलम्.. 15.32 ..
1.3.m: They reach the highest world; no deliberation is needed here. / Therefore, that ill-behaved one indeed received the fruit of his deed.

1.3.s:
sa pradhārya tadā sarve lokapālāstvarānvitāḥ..
bṛhaspatimupāgamya sarvamātmani dhiṣṭhitam..
kathayāmāsuravyagrā iṃdrasya ca guruṃ prati.. 15.33 ..
1.3.d:
स प्रधार्य तदा सर्वे लोकपालास्त्वरान्विताः..
बृहस्पतिमुपागम्य सर्वमात्मनि धिष्ठितम्..
कथयामासुरव्यग्रा इंद्रस्य च गुरुं प्रति.. 15.33 ..
1.3.m: Having deliberated thus, all the guardians of the quarters, full of haste, / approached Bṛhaspati, and composedly told everything / that weighed upon their minds to Indra's guru.

1.3.s:
devairuktaṃ vaco viprā niśamya ca bṛhaspatiḥ..
arājakaṃ ca saṃprāptaṃ ciṃtayāmāsa buddhimān.. 15.34 ..
1.3.d:
देवैरुक्तं वचो विप्रा निशम्य च बृहस्पतिः..
अराजकं च संप्राप्तं चिंतयामास बुद्धिमान्.. 15.34 ..
1.3.m: Hearing the words spoken by the gods, O brahmins, / the wise Bṛhaspati pondered the kingless state that had arisen:

1.3.s:
kiṃ kāryaṃ cādya kartavyaṃ kathaṃ śreyo bhaviṣyati..
devānāṃ cādya lokānāmṛṣīṇāṃ bhāvitātmanām.. 15.35 ..
1.3.d:
किं कार्यं चाद्य कर्तव्यं कथं श्रेयो भविष्यति..
देवानां चाद्य लोकानामृषीणां भावितात्मनाम्.. 15.35 ..
1.3.m: “What is to be done now? How will there be welfare / today for the gods, the worlds, and the contemplative ṛṣis?”

1.3.s:
manasaiva ca tatsarvaṃ kāryākāryaṃ vicārya ca..
jagāma śakraṃ tvarito devaiḥ saha mahāyaśāḥ.. 15.36 ..
1.3.d:
मनसैव च तत्सर्वं कार्याकार्यं विचार्य च..
जगाम शक्रं त्वरितो देवैः सह महायशाः.. 15.36 ..
1.3.m: Deliberating in his mind all that should and should not be done, / the highly renowned one quickly went with the gods to Śakra.

1.3.s:
prāpto jalāśayaṃ taṃ ca yatrāste hi puraṃdaraḥ..
yasya tīre sthitā hatyā caṃḍālīva bhayāvahā.. 15.37 ..
1.3.d:
प्राप्तो जलाशयं तं च यत्रास्ते हि पुरंदरः..
यस्य तीरे स्थिता हत्या चंडालीव भयावहा.. 15.37 ..
1.3.m: He arrived at that pool where Purandara indeed sat, / on the bank of which the murder [of a brahmin] stood, fearful like an outcaste woman.

1.3.s:
tatroviṣṭāste sarve devā ṛṣigaṇānvitāḥ..
āhvānaṃ ca kṛtaṃ tasya śakrasya guruṇā svayam.. 15.38 ..
1.3.d:
तत्रोविष्टास्ते सर्वे देवा ऋषिगणान्विताः..
आह्वानं च कृतं तस्य शक्रस्य गुरुणा स्वयम्.. 15.38 ..
1.3.m: All those gods accompanied by the groups of ṛṣis sat down there, / and Śakra was summoned by the guru himself.

1.3.s:
samutthitastataḥ śakro dadarśa svaguruṃ tadā..
bāṣpapūritavaktro hi bṛhaspatimabhāṣata.. 15.39 ..
1.3.d:
समुत्थितस्ततः शक्रो ददर्श स्वगुरुं तदा..
बाष्पपूरितवक्त्रो हि बृहस्पतिमभाषत.. 15.39 ..
1.3.m: Śakra then rose up and saw his own guru; / with his face filled with tears, he addressed Bṛhaspati.

1.3.s:
praṇipatya ca tatratyānkṛtāñjalirabhāṣata..
tadā dīnamukho bhūtvā manasā saṃvimṛśya ca.. 15.40 ..
1.3.d:
प्रणिपत्य च तत्रत्यान्कृताञ्जलिरभाषत..
तदा दीनमुखो भूत्वा मनसा संविमृश्य च.. 15.40 ..
1.3.m: Having bowed down to those present there, with folded hands he spoke; / then, having become dejected in face and reflecting in his mind:

1.3.s:
svayameva kṛtaṃ pūrvamajñānalakṣaṇaṃ mahat..
adhunaiva mayā kāryaṃ kiṃ kartavyaṃ vada prabho.. 15.41 ..
1.3.d:
स्वयमेव कृतं पूर्वमज्ञानलक्षणं महत्..
अधुनैव मया कार्यं किं कर्तव्यं वद प्रभो.. 15.41 ..
1.3.m: “By myself alone a great deed characterized by ignorance was committed previously; / tell me, O Lord, what ought to be done by me right now?”

1.3.s:
prahasyovāca bhagavānbṛhaspati rudāradhīḥ..
purā tvayā kṛtaṃ yacca tasyedaṃ karmaṇaḥ phalam.. 15.42 ..
1.3.d:
प्रहस्योवाच भगवान्बृहस्पति रुदारधीः..
पुरा त्वया कृतं यच्च तस्येदं कर्मणः फलम्.. 15.42 ..
1.3.m: Smiling, the noble-minded, venerable Bṛhaspati said: / “This is the fruit of that deed which was done by you in the past.

1.3.s:
māṃ ca uddiśya bho iṃdra tadbhogādeva saṃkṣayaḥ..
prāyaścitaṃ hi hatyāyā na dṛṣṭaṃ smṛtikāribhiḥ.. 15.43 ..
1.3.d:
मां च उद्दिश्य भो इंद्र तद्भोगादेव संक्षयः..
प्रायश्चितं हि हत्याया न दृष्टं स्मृतिकारिभिः.. 15.43 ..
1.3.m: And in regard to me, O Indra, its destruction comes only through experiencing it; / indeed, no expiation for murder has been seen by the authors of the legal texts.

1.3.s:
ajñānato hi yajjātaṃ pāpaṃ tasya pratikriyā..
kathitā dharmmaśāstrajñaiḥ sakāmasya na vidyate.. 15.44 ..
1.3.d:
अज्ञानतो हि यज्जातं पापं तस्य प्रतिक्रिया..
कथिता धर्म्मशास्त्रज्ञैः सकामस्य न विद्यते.. 15.44 ..
1.3.m: A remedy has been declared by the knowers of the treatises on dharma / for a sin committed through ignorance, but none exists for intentional [sin].

1.3.s:
sakāmena kṛtaṃ pāpamakāmaṃ naiva jāyate..
tābhyāṃ viṣayabhedena prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate.. 15.45 ..
1.3.d:
सकामेन कृतं पापमकामं नैव जायते..
ताभ्यां विषयभेदेन प्रायश्चित्तं विधीयते.. 15.45 ..
1.3.m: A sin committed intentionally does not become unintentional; / expiation is prescribed according to the distinction between these two cases.

1.3.s:
maraṇāṃto vidhiḥ kāryo kāmena hi kṛtena hi..
ajñānajanite pāpe prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyate.. 15.46 ..
1.3.d:
मरणांतो विधिः कार्यो कामेन हि कृतेन हि..
अज्ञानजनिते पापे प्रायश्चित्तं विधीयते.. 15.46 ..
1.3.m: A rite ending in death must be performed for what was committed intentionally; / expiation is prescribed for a sin produced by ignorance.

1.3.s:
tasmāttvayā kṛtaṃ yacca svayameva hato dvijaḥ..
purohitaśca vidvāṃśca tasmānnāsti pratikriyā.. 15.47 ..
1.3.d:
तस्मात्त्वया कृतं यच्च स्वयमेव हतो द्विजः..
पुरोहितश्च विद्वांश्च तस्मान्नास्ति प्रतिक्रिया.. 15.47 ..
1.3.m: Therefore, regarding what was done by you—a brahmin was slain by yourself, / one who was your family priest and learned—there is no remedy for it.

1.3.s: yāvanmaraṇamapyeti tāvadapsu sthiro bhava.. 15.48 ..
1.3.d: यावन्मरणमप्येति तावदप्सु स्थिरो भव.. 15.48 ..
1.3.m: Remain still in the waters until death approaches.

1.3.s:
śatāśvamedhasaṃjñaṃ ca yatphalaṃ tava durmate..
tannaṣṭaṃ tatkṣaṇādeva ghātito hi dvijo yadā.. 15.49 ..
1.3.d:
शताश्वमेधसंज्ञं च यत्फलं तव दुर्मते..
तन्नष्टं तत्क्षणादेव घातितो हि द्विजो यदा.. 15.49 ..
1.3.m: That fruit of yours known as [the reward of] a hundred horse-sacrifices, O foolish one, / perished at that very instant when the brahmin was slain.

1.3.s:
sacchidre ca yathā toyaṃ na tiṣṭhati ghaṭe'ṇvapi..
tathaiva sukṛtaṃ pāpe hīyate ca pradakṣiṇam.. 15.50 ..
1.3.d:
सच्छिद्रे च यथा तोयं न तिष्ठति घटेऽण्वपि..
तथैव सुकृतं पापे हीयते च प्रदक्षिणम्.. 15.50 ..
1.3.m: Just as not even a drop of water remains in a jar full of holes, / even so good merit is depleted in the face of sin.

1.3.s:
tasmācca daivasaṃyogātprāptaṃ svargādikaṃ ca yaiḥ..
yathoktaṃ tadbhavetteṣāṃ dharmiṣṭhānāṃ na saṃśayaḥ.. 15.51 ..
1.3.d:
तस्माच्च दैवसंयोगात्प्राप्तं स्वर्गादिकं च यैः..
यथोक्तं तद्भवेत्तेषां धर्मिष्ठानां न संशयः.. 15.51 ..
1.3.m: Therefore, whatever heaven and the like is attained by those through the conjunction of destiny / becomes as stated for those who are righteous, without doubt.”

1.3.s:
etacchrutvā vacastasya śakro vacanamabravīt..
kukarmaṇā madīyena prāptametanna saṃśayaḥ.. 15.52 ..
1.3.d:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा वचस्तस्य शक्रो वचनमब्रवीत्..
कुकर्मणा मदीयेन प्राप्तमेतन्न संशयः.. 15.52 ..
1.3.m: Hearing this speech of his, Śakra spoke these words: / “This has been obtained through my own evil deed, there is no doubt.

1.3.s:
amarāvatī māśu tvaṃ gaccha devarṣibiḥ saha..
lokānāṃ kāryasiddhyarthe devānāṃ ca bṛhaspate..
iṃdraṃ kuru mahābhāga yaste manasi rocate.. 15.53 ..
1.3.d:
अमरावती माशु त्वं गच्छ देवर्षिबिः सह..
लोकानां कार्यसिद्ध्यर्थे देवानां च बृहस्पते..
इंद्रं कुरु महाभाग यस्ते मनसि रोचते.. 15.53 ..
1.3.m: Go quickly to Amarāvatī along with the divine ṛṣis; / for the sake of the accomplishment of the tasks of the worlds and of the gods, O Bṛhaspati, / make an Indra, O highly fortunate one, whomever your mind pleases.

1.3.s:
yathā mṛtastathā haṃ vai brahmahatyāvṛto mahān..
rāgadveṣasamutthena pāpenāsmi pariplutaḥ.. 15.54 ..
1.3.d:
यथा मृतस्तथा हं वै ब्रह्महत्यावृतो महान्..
रागद्वेषसमुत्थेन पापेनास्मि परिप्लुतः.. 15.54 ..
1.3.m: As one dead, so indeed am I, great though I was, surrounded by the murder of a brahmin; / I am overwhelmed by the sin arising from passion and hatred.

1.3.s:
tasmāttvarānvitā yūyaṃ devarājānamāśuḥ vai..
kurvatu madanujñātāḥ satyaṃ prativadāmi vaḥ.. 15.55 ..
1.3.d:
तस्मात्त्वरान्विता यूयं देवराजानमाशुः वै..
कुर्वतु मदनुज्ञाताः सत्यं प्रतिवदामि वः.. 15.55 ..
1.3.m: Therefore, full of haste, quickly make a king of gods, / permitted by me; I tell you the truth.”

1.3.s:
evamuktāstadā sarve bṛhaspatipurogamāḥ..
etyāmarāvatīṃ tūrṇaṃ puraṃdaraviceṣṭitam..
kathayāmāsuravyagrā śacīṃ prati yathā tathā.. 15.56 ..
1.3.d:
एवमुक्तास्तदा सर्वे बृहस्पतिपुरोगमाः..
एत्यामरावतीं तूर्णं पुरंदरविचेष्टितम्..
कथयामासुरव्यग्रा शचीं प्रति यथा तथा.. 15.56 ..
1.3.m: Addressed thus, all of them led by Bṛhaspati / went quickly to Amarāvatī and, composed, told Śacī / everything about Purandara's deed just as it happened,

1.3.s: rājyasya hetoḥ kiṃ kāryaṃ vimṛśaṃtaḥ parasparam.. 15.57 ..
1.3.d: राज्यस्य हेतोः किं कार्यं विमृशंतः परस्परम्.. 15.57 ..
1.3.m: deliberating among one another: “What should be done for the sake of the kingdom?”

1.3.s:
evaṃ vimṛśyamānānāṃ devānāṃ tatra nāradaḥ..
yadṛcchayāgatastatra devarṣiramitadyutiḥ.. 15.58 ..
1.3.d:
एवं विमृश्यमानानां देवानां तत्र नारदः..
यदृच्छयागतस्तत्र देवर्षिरमितद्युतिः.. 15.58 ..
1.3.m: While the gods were deliberating thus, the divine ṛṣi Nārada, / of boundless splendor, arrived there by chance.

1.3.s:
uvāca pūjito devānkasmādyūyaṃ vicetasaḥ..
tenoktāḥ kathayāmāsuḥ sarvaṃ śakrasya ceṣṭitam.. 15.59 ..
1.3.d:
उवाच पूजितो देवान्कस्माद्यूयं विचेतसः..
तेनोक्ताः कथयामासुः सर्वं शक्रस्य चेष्टितम्.. 15.59 ..
1.3.m: Worshipped [by them], he said to the gods: “Why are you distraught?” / Asked by him, they recounted all of Śakra's conduct.

1.3.s:
gatamiṃdrasya ceṃdratvamenasā parameṇa tu..
tataḥ provāca tāndevāndevarṣirnārado vacaḥ.. 15.60 ..
1.3.d:
गतमिंद्रस्य चेंद्रत्वमेनसा परमेण तु..
ततः प्रोवाच तान्देवान्देवर्षिर्नारदो वचः.. 15.60 ..
1.3.m: And Indra’s lordship over the gods was lost due to supreme sin. / Then the celestial seer Nārada spoke [these] words to the gods:

1.3.s:
yūyaṃ devāśca sarvajñāstapasā vikrameṇa ca..
tasmādiṃdro hi kartavyo nahuṣaḥ somavaṃśajaḥ.. 15.61 ..
1.3.d:
यूयं देवाश्च सर्वज्ञास्तपसा विक्रमेण च..
तस्मादिंद्रो हि कर्तव्यो नहुषः सोमवंशजः.. 15.61 ..
1.3.m: “You gods are all-knowing through austerity and valour. / Therefore, Nahuṣa, born of the lunar dynasty, must be made Indra.

1.3.s:
so'sminrāṣṭre pratiṣṭhāpyastvaritenaiva nirjarāḥ..
ekonamaśvamedhānāṃ śataṃ tena mahātmanā..
kṛtamasti mahābhāgā nahuṣeṇa ca yajvanā.. 15.62 ..
1.3.d:
सोऽस्मिन्राष्ट्रे प्रतिष्ठाप्यस्त्वरितेनैव निर्जराः..
एकोनमश्वमेधानां शतं तेन महात्मना..
कृतमस्ति महाभागा नहुषेण च यज्वना.. 15.62 ..
1.3.m: O immortals, he must be established in this realm immediately! / Ninety-nine horse-sacrifices have been performed / by that great-souled sacrificer Nahuṣa, O fortunate ones!”

1.3.s:
śacyā śrutaṃ ca tadvākyaṃ nāradasya mukhodgatam..
gatāṃtaḥpuramavyagrā bāṣpapūritalocanā.. 15.63 ..
1.3.d:
शच्या श्रुतं च तद्वाक्यं नारदस्य मुखोद्गतम्..
गतांतःपुरमव्यग्रा बाष्पपूरितलोचना.. 15.63 ..
1.3.m: And that statement issuing from the mouth of Nārada was heard by Śacī. / Undistracted, she went to the inner quarters with her eyes filled with tears.

1.3.s: nāradasya vacaḥ śrutvā sarve devānvamodayan.. 15.64 ..
1.3.d: नारदस्य वचः श्रुत्वा सर्वे देवान्वमोदयन्.. 15.64 ..
1.3.m: Having heard the words of Nārada, all the gods approved.

1.3.s:
nahuṣaṃ rājyamāroḍhumaikapadyena te yadā..
ānīto hi tadā rājā nahuṣo hyamarāvatīm.. 15.65 ..
1.3.d:
नहुषं राज्यमारोढुमैकपद्येन ते यदा..
आनीतो हि तदा राजा नहुषो ह्यमरावतीम्.. 15.65 ..
1.3.m: When they [decided] with one voice that Nahuṣa should ascend the throne, / then King Nahuṣa was indeed brought to Amarāvatī.

1.3.s:
rājyaṃ dattaṃ maheṃdrasya suraiḥ sarvairmaharṣibhiḥ..
tadāgastyādayaḥ sarve nahuṣaṃ paryupāsata.. 15.66 ..
1.3.d:
राज्यं दत्तं महेंद्रस्य सुरैः सर्वैर्महर्षिभिः..
तदागस्त्यादयः सर्वे नहुषं पर्युपासत.. 15.66 ..
1.3.m: The kingdom of Mahendra was given [to him] by all the gods and great seers; / then Agastya and all the others attended upon Nahuṣa.

1.3.s:
gaṃdharvāpsaraso yakṣā vidyādharamahoragāḥ..
yakṣāḥ suparṇāḥ patagā ye cānye svargavāsinaḥ.. 15.67 ..
1.3.d:
गंधर्वाप्सरसो यक्षा विद्याधरमहोरगाः..
यक्षाः सुपर्णाः पतगा ये चान्ये स्वर्गवासिनः.. 15.67 ..
1.3.m: Gandharvas, apsarases, yakṣas, vidyādharas, great serpents, / yakṣas, suparṇas, birds, and whatever other dwellers of heaven [there were]—

1.3.s:
tadā mahotsavo jāto devapuryāṃ niraṃtaraḥ..
śaṃkhatūryamṛdaṃgāni nedurduṃdubhayaḥ samam.. 15.68 ..
1.3.d:
तदा महोत्सवो जातो देवपुर्यां निरंतरः..
शंखतूर्यमृदंगानि नेदुर्दुंदुभयः समम्.. 15.68 ..
1.3.m: then a continuous great festival took place in the city of the gods. / Conches, clarions, mṛdaṅga drums, and kettledrums sounded together.

1.3.s:
gāyakāśca jagustatra tathā vādyāni vādakāḥ..
nartakā nanṛtustatra tathā rājyamahotsave.. 15.69 ..
1.3.d:
गायकाश्च जगुस्तत्र तथा वाद्यानि वादकाः..
नर्तका ननृतुस्तत्र तथा राज्यमहोत्सवे.. 15.69 ..
1.3.m: And singers sang there, and instrumentalists [played] instruments; / dancers danced there in that great festival of kingship.

1.3.s: abhiṣiktastadā tatra bṛhaspatipurogamaiḥ.. 15.70 ..
1.3.d: अभिषिक्तस्तदा तत्र बृहस्पतिपुरोगमैः.. 15.70 ..
1.3.m: He was then consecrated there by those headed by Bṛhaspati,

1.3.s:
arcito devasūktaiśca yathā vadgrahapūjanam..
kṛtavāṃścaiva ṛṣibhirvidvadbhirbhāvitātmabhiḥ.. 15.71 ..
1.3.d:
अर्चितो देवसूक्तैश्च यथा वद्ग्रहपूजनम्..
कृतवांश्चैव ऋषिभिर्विद्वद्भिर्भावितात्मभिः.. 15.71 ..
1.3.m: honoured with divine hymns, and duly performed the worship of the planets / through the learned seers of purified souls.

1.3.s:
tathā ca sarvaiḥ paripūjito mahānrājā surāṇāṃ nahuṣastadānīm..
iṃdrāsane ceṃd samānarūpaḥ saṃstūyamānaḥ parameṇa varcasā.. 15.72 ..
1.3.d:
तथा च सर्वैः परिपूजितो महान्राजा सुराणां नहुषस्तदानीम्..
इंद्रासने चेंद् समानरूपः संस्तूयमानः परमेण वर्चसा.. 15.72 ..
1.3.m: And thus worshipfully honoured by all, the great king of the gods, Nahuṣa, then, / equal in form to Indra on Indra’s throne, was praised with supreme splendour.

1.3.s:
sugaṃdhadīpaiśca suvāsasā yuto'laṃkārabhogaiḥ suvirājitāṃgaḥ..
babhau tadānīṃ nahuṣo munīdraiḥ saṃstūyamāno hi tathā'mareṃdraiḥ.. 15.73 ..
1.3.d:
सुगंधदीपैश्च सुवाससा युतोऽलंकारभोगैः सुविराजितांगः..
बभौ तदानीं नहुषो मुनीद्रैः संस्तूयमानो हि तथाऽमरेंद्रैः.. 15.73 ..
1.3.m: Endowed with fragrant lamps and fine garments, his limbs adorned with ornaments and luxuries, / Nahuṣa shone then, praised by the foremost sages and likewise by the lords of the immortals.

1.3.s:
iti paramakalānvito'sau suramunivaragaṇaiśca pūjyamānaḥ..
nahuṣanṛpavaro'bhavattadānīṃ hṛdi mahatā hṛcchayenataptaḥ.. 15.74 ..
1.3.d:
इति परमकलान्वितोऽसौ सुरमुनिवरगणैश्च पूज्यमानः..
नहुषनृपवरोऽभवत्तदानीं हृदि महता हृच्छयेनतप्तः.. 15.74 ..
1.3.m: Thus endowed with supreme elegance, honoured by the hosts of gods and foremost sages, / that excellent king Nahuṣa became afflicted in his heart by intense desire.

1.3.s:
..nahuṣa uvāca..
iṃdrāṇī kathamadyaiva nāyāti mama sannidhau..
tāṃ cāhvayata śīghraṃ bho mā vilaṃbitumarhatha.. 15.75 ..
1.3.d:
..नहुष उवाच..
इंद्राणी कथमद्यैव नायाति मम सन्निधौ..
तां चाह्वयत शीघ्रं भो मा विलंबितुमर्हथ.. 15.75 ..
1.3.m: Nahuṣa said: / “Why does Indrāṇī not come to my presence this very day? / Summon her quickly! Ho, you must not delay!”

1.3.s:
nahupasya vacaḥ śrutvā bṛhaspatirudāradhīḥ..
śacībhavanamāsādya uvāca ca savistaram.. 15.76 ..
1.3.d:
नहुपस्य वचः श्रुत्वा बृहस्पतिरुदारधीः..
शचीभवनमासाद्य उवाच च सविस्तरम्.. 15.76 ..
1.3.m: Hearing the words of Nahuṣa, the noble-minded Bṛhaspati, / having reached the residence of Śacī, spoke in detail:

1.3.s:
śakrasya durnimittena hyanīto nahuṣo'tra vai..
rājyārte bhāmini tvaṃ ca arddhāsanagatā bhava.. 15.77 ..
1.3.d:
शक्रस्य दुर्निमित्तेन ह्यनीतो नहुषोऽत्र वै..
राज्यार्ते भामिनि त्वं च अर्द्धासनगता भव.. 15.77 ..
1.3.m: “Owing to the misfortune of Śakra, Nahuṣa has indeed been brought here. / For the sake of the kingdom, O radiant lady, share his throne!”

1.3.s:
śacī prahasya covāca bṛhaspatimakalmaṣam..
asau na paripūrṇo hi yajñaiḥ śakrāsane sthitaḥ..
ekonamaśvamedhānāṃ śataṃ kṛtamanena vai.. 15.78 ..
1.3.d:
शची प्रहस्य चोवाच बृहस्पतिमकल्मषम्..
असौ न परिपूर्णो हि यज्ञैः शक्रासने स्थितः..
एकोनमश्वमेधानां शतं कृतमनेन वै.. 15.78 ..
1.3.m: Śacī laughed and said to the faultless Bṛhaspati: / “He, seated upon Śakra’s throne, is indeed not fulfilled with sacrifices; / a hundred horse-sacrifices minus one have been performed by him.

1.3.s:
tasmānna yogyo prahasya covāca bṛhaspatimakalpaṇaṣam..
asau na paripūrṇo hi yajñaiḥ śakrāsane sthitaḥ..
avāhyavāhanenaiva atrāgatya labheta mām.. 15.79 ..
1.3.d:
तस्मान्न योग्यो प्रहस्य चोवाच बृहस्पतिमकल्पणषम्..
असौ न परिपूर्णो हि यज्ञैः शक्रासने स्थितः..
अवाह्यवाहनेनैव अत्रागत्य लभेत माम्.. 15.79 ..
1.3.m: Therefore he is not fit […] / He, seated upon Śakra’s throne, is not fulfilled with sacrifices; / only by coming here upon a mount not to be ridden may he obtain me.”

1.3.s:
tatheti gatvā tvarito bṛhaspatiruvāca tam..
nahuṣaṃ kāmasaṃtaptaṃ śacyoktaṃ ca yathātatham.. 15.80 ..
1.3.d:
तथेति गत्वा त्वरितो बृहस्पतिरुवाच तम्..
नहुषं कामसंतप्तं शच्योक्तं च यथातथम्.. 15.80 ..
1.3.m: Saying “So be it,” Bṛhaspati went quickly and told Nahuṣa, / who was burning with desire, exactly what had been spoken by Śacī.

1.3.s:
tatheti matvā rājāsau nahuṣaḥ kāmamohitaḥ..
vimṛśya parayā buddhyā avāhyaṃ kiṃ praśasyate.. 15.81 ..
1.3.d:
तथेति मत्वा राजासौ नहुषः काममोहितः..
विमृश्य परया बुद्ध्या अवाह्यं किं प्रशस्यते.. 15.81 ..
1.3.m: Thinking “So be it,” that king Nahuṣa, infatuated by desire, / reflected with superior intellect: “What is praised as not to be ridden?”

1.3.s:
sa buddhyā ca ciraṃ smṛtvā brāhmaṇāścatapasvinaḥ..
avāhyāśca bhavaṃtyasmādātmānaṃ vāhayāmyaham.. 15.82 ..
1.3.d:
स बुद्ध्या च चिरं स्मृत्वा ब्राह्मणाश्चतपस्विनः..
अवाह्याश्च भवंत्यस्मादात्मानं वाहयाम्यहम्.. 15.82 ..
1.3.m: Having reflected long with his intellect: “Brāhmaṇas and ascetics / are not to be ridden; therefore, I shall have myself carried [by them]—

1.3.s:
dvābhyāṃ ca tasyāḥ prāptyarthamiti me hṛdi vartate..
śibikāṃ ca dadau tābhyāṃ dvijābhyāṃ kāmamohitaḥ.. 15.83 ..
1.3.d:
द्वाभ्यां च तस्याः प्राप्त्यर्थमिति मे हृदि वर्तते..
शिबिकां च ददौ ताभ्यां द्विजाभ्यां काममोहितः.. 15.83 ..
1.3.m: by two [of them] in order to obtain her; this is what is in my heart.” / Infatuated by desire, he gave a palanquin to two twice-borns.

1.3.s:
upaviśya tadā tasyāṃ śivabikāyāṃ samāhitaḥ..
sarpasarpeti vacanānnodayāmāsa tau tadā.. 15.84 ..
1.3.d:
उपविश्य तदा तस्यां शिवबिकायां समाहितः..
सर्पसर्पेति वचनान्नोदयामास तौ तदा.. 15.84 ..
1.3.m: Sitting then attentively in that palanquin, / he urged them on with the words: “Move, move!”

1.3.s:
agastyaḥ śibikāvāhī tataḥ kruddho'śapannṛpam..
viprāṇāmavamaṃtā tvamunmatto'jagaro bhava.. 15.85 ..
1.3.d:
अगस्त्यः शिबिकावाही ततः क्रुद्धोऽशपन्नृपम्..
विप्राणामवमंता त्वमुन्मत्तोऽजगरो भव.. 15.85 ..
1.3.m: Then Agastya, bearer of the palanquin, became enraged and cursed the king: / “You scorner of brāhmaṇas! Become an intoxicated python!”

1.3.s:
śāpoktimātrato rājā patito brāhmaṇasya hi..
tatraivājagaro bhūtvā vipraśāpo duratyayaḥ.. 15.86 ..
1.3.d:
शापोक्तिमात्रतो राजा पतितो ब्राह्मणस्य हि..
तत्रैवाजगरो भूत्वा विप्रशापो दुरत्ययः.. 15.86 ..
1.3.m: From the mere utterance of the curse, the king fell before the brāhmaṇa, / turning into a python right there; a brāhmaṇa’s curse is insurmountable.

1.3.s:
yathā hi nahuṣo jātastathā sarve'pi tādṛśāḥ..
viprāṇāmavamānena patinti niraye'śucau.. 15.87 ..
1.3.d:
यथा हि नहुषो जातस्तथा सर्वेऽपि तादृशाः..
विप्राणामवमानेन पतिन्ति निरयेऽशुचौ.. 15.87 ..
1.3.m: Just as Nahuṣa became, so all who are like him / fall into an impure hell through disrespect toward brāhmaṇas.

1.3.s:
tasmāsarvaprayatnena padaṃ prāpya vicakṣaṇaiḥ..
apramattairnarairbhāvyamihāmutra ca labdhaye.. 15.88 ..
1.3.d:
तस्मासर्वप्रयत्नेन पदं प्राप्य विचक्षणैः..
अप्रमत्तैर्नरैर्भाव्यमिहामुत्र च लब्धये.. 15.88 ..
1.3.m: Therefore, having attained a station, wise and heedful / men should make every effort to attain [good] here and in the hereafter.

1.3.s:
tathaiva nahuṣaḥ sarppo jātoraṇye mahābhaye..
evaṃ caivābhavattatra devaloke hyarājakam.. 15.89 ..
1.3.d:
तथैव नहुषः सर्प्पो जातोरण्ये महाभये..
एवं चैवाभवत्तत्र देवलोके ह्यराजकम्.. 15.89 ..
1.3.m: Just so, Nahuṣa became a serpent in a very dreadful forest. / And thus there was kinglessness in the realm of the gods.

1.3.s:
tathaiva te surāḥ sarve vismayāviṣṭacetasaḥ..
aho bata mahatkaṣṭaṃ prāptaṃ rājñā hyanena vai.. 15.90 ..
1.3.d:
तथैव ते सुराः सर्वे विस्मयाविष्टचेतसः..
अहो बत महत्कष्टं प्राप्तं राज्ञा ह्यनेन वै.. 15.90 ..
1.3.m: Likewise, all those gods, their minds overcome with astonishment, [said]: / “Alas, what great misery has indeed been attained by this king!

1.3.s:
na martya loko na svargo jāto hyasya durātmanaḥ..
satāmavajñayā sadyaḥ sukṛtaṃ dagdhameva hi.. 15.91 ..
1.3.d:
न मर्त्य लोको न स्वर्गो जातो ह्यस्य दुरात्मनः..
सतामवज्ञया सद्यः सुकृतं दग्धमेव हि.. 15.91 ..
1.3.m: Neither the mortal world nor heaven remains for this wicked soul; / through disrespect of the virtuous, his good deeds are instantly burnt up!”

1.3.s:
yājñiko hyaparo loke kathyatāṃ ca mahāmune..
tadovāca mahātejā nārado munisattamaḥ.. 15.92 ..
1.3.d:
याज्ञिको ह्यपरो लोके कथ्यतां च महामुने..
तदोवाच महातेजा नारदो मुनिसत्तमः.. 15.92 ..
1.3.m: “Let another performer of sacrifices in the world be mentioned, O great sage!” / Then the glorious Nārada, the best of sages, said:

1.3.s:
yayātiṃ ca mahābhāgā ānayadhvaṃ tvarānvitāḥ..
devadūtāstu vai tūrṇaṃ yayātiṃ drutamānayan.. 15.93 ..
1.3.d:
ययातिं च महाभागा आनयध्वं त्वरान्विताः..
देवदूतास्तु वै तूर्णं ययातिं द्रुतमानयन्.. 15.93 ..
1.3.m: “Bring Yayāti with haste, O fortunate ones!” / Then the divine messengers swiftly brought Yayāti in haste.

1.3.s:
vimānamāruhya tadā mahātmā yayau divaṃ devadūtaiḥ sametaḥ..
puraskṛto devavaraistadānīṃ tathoragairyakṣagaṃdharvasiddhaiḥ.. 15.94 ..
1.3.d:
विमानमारुह्य तदा महात्मा ययौ दिवं देवदूतैः समेतः..
पुरस्कृतो देववरैस्तदानीं तथोरगैर्यक्षगंधर्वसिद्धैः.. 15.94 ..
1.3.m: Mounting the aerial chariot, the great-souled one then went to heaven accompanied by the divine messengers, / honoured then by the foremost gods, and likewise by serpents, yakṣas, gandharvas, and siddhas.

1.3.s:
āyātaḥ so'marāvatyāṃ tridaśairabhitoṣitaḥ..
iṃdrāsane copaviṣṭo babhāṣe ca sa satvaram.. 15.95 ..
1.3.d:
आयातः सोऽमरावत्यां त्रिदशैरभितोषितः..
इंद्रासने चोपविष्टो बभाषे च स सत्वरम्.. 15.95 ..
1.3.m: Arriving at Amarāvatī, he was gratified by the thirty [gods]; / and seated upon Indra’s throne, he spoke promptly.

1.3.s:
nāradenaivamuktastu tvaṃ rājā yājñiko hyasi..
satāmavajñayā prāpto nahuṣo daṃdaśūkatām.. 15.96 ..
1.3.d:
नारदेनैवमुक्तस्तु त्वं राजा याज्ञिको ह्यसि..
सतामवज्ञया प्राप्तो नहुषो दंदशूकताम्.. 15.96 ..
1.3.m: Addressed thus by Nārada: “You are indeed a sacrifice-performing king; / Nahuṣa met the condition of a serpent through disrespect of the virtuous.

1.3.s:
ye prāpnuvaṃti dharmiṣṭhā daivena paramaṃ padam..
prāktanenaiva mūḍhāste na paśyaṃti śubhāśubham.. 15.97 ..
1.3.d:
ये प्राप्नुवंति धर्मिष्ठा दैवेन परमं पदम्..
प्राक्तनेनैव मूढास्ते न पश्यंति शुभाशुभम्.. 15.97 ..
1.3.m: Those righteous ones who attain the supreme station through past destiny, / deluded, do not perceive the auspicious and the inauspicious;

1.3.s: pataṃti narake ghore stabdhā vai nātra saṃśayaḥ.. 15.98 ..
1.3.d: पतंति नरके घोरे स्तब्धा वै नात्र संशयः.. 15.98 ..
1.3.m: arrogant, they fall into a dreadful hell; of this there is no doubt.”

1.3.s:
..yayātiruvāca..
yaiḥ kṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ teṣāṃ vighnaḥ prajāyate..
alpakatvena devarṣe viddhi sarvaṃ paraṃ mama.. 15.99 ..
1.3.d:
..ययातिरुवाच..
यैः कृतं पुण्यं तेषां विघ्नः प्रजायते..
अल्पकत्वेन देवर्षे विद्धि सर्वं परं मम.. 15.99 ..
1.3.m: Yayāti said: / “An obstacle arises for those by whom merit is done / in small measure, O divine seer; know all of mine to be supreme!

1.3.s:
mahādānāni dattāni annadānayutāni ca..
godānāni bahūnyeva bhūmidānayutāni ca.. 15.100 ..
1.3.d:
महादानानि दत्तानि अन्नदानयुतानि च..
गोदानानि बहून्येव भूमिदानयुतानि च.. 15.100 ..
1.3.m: Great gifts have been given, along with gifts of food, / many gifts of cows, along with gifts of land.

1.3.s:
tathaiva sarvāṇyapi cottamāni dānāni coktāni manīṣibhiryadā..
etāni sarvāṇi mayā tadaiva dattāni kāle ca mahāvidhānataḥ.. 15.101 ..
1.3.d:
तथैव सर्वाण्यपि चोत्तमानि दानानि चोक्तानि मनीषिभिर्यदा..
एतानि सर्वाणि मया तदैव दत्तानि काले च महाविधानतः.. 15.101 ..
1.3.m: Likewise, all the highest gifts that have been proclaimed by the wise— / all of these were given by me at the right time, according to the great rites.”

1.3.s:
yajñairiṣṭaṃ vājapeyātirātrairjyotiṣṭomai rājasūyādibhiśca..
śāstraproktairaśvamedhādibhiśca yūpaireṣālaṃkṛtā bhūḥ samaṃtāt.. 15.102 ..
1.3.d:
यज्ञैरिष्टं वाजपेयातिरात्रैर्ज्योतिष्टोमै राजसूयादिभिश्च..
शास्त्रप्रोक्तैरश्वमेधादिभिश्च यूपैरेषालंकृता भूः समंतात्.. 15.102 ..
1.3.m: Sacrifices were offered by me: Vājapeyas, Atirātras, Jyotiṣṭomas, and Rājasūyas, / and with the horse sacrifices prescribed by sacred lore, this earth was adorned on all sides with sacrificial posts. (15.102)

1.3.s:
devadevo jagannātha iṣṭo yajñairanekaśaḥ..
gālavāya pure dattā kanyā tveṣā ca mādhavī.. 15.103 ..
1.3.d:
देवदेवो जगन्नाथ इष्टो यज्ञैरनेकशः..
गालवाय पुरे दत्ता कन्या त्वेषा च माधवी.. 15.103 ..
1.3.m: The god of gods, the lord of the universe, was worshiped through manifold sacrifices. / In ancient times, this maiden Mādhavī was given to Gālava, (15.103)

1.3.s:
patnītvena caturbhyaśca dattāḥ kanyā mune tadā..
gālavasya gurorarthe viśvāmitrasya dhīmataḥ.. 15.104 ..
1.3.d:
पत्नीत्वेन चतुर्भ्यश्च दत्ताः कन्या मुने तदा..
गालवस्य गुरोरर्थे विश्वामित्रस्य धीमतः.. 15.104 ..
1.3.m: and then she was given to four [kings] as their wife, O sage, / for the sake of Gālava's preceptor, the wise Viśvāmitra. (15.104)

1.3.s:
evaṃ bhūtānyanekāni sukṛtāni mayā purā..
mahāṃti ca bahūnyeva tāni vaktuṃ na pāryate.. 15.105 ..
1.3.d:
एवं भूतान्यनेकानि सुकृतानि मया पुरा..
महांति च बहून्येव तानि वक्तुं न पार्यते.. 15.105 ..
1.3.m: Many such great and virtuous deeds were done by me in the past; / indeed, they are so numerous that it is impossible to recount them. (15.105)

1.3.s:
bhūyaḥ pṛṣṭaḥ sarvadevaiḥ sa rājā kṛtaṃ sarvaṃ guptameva yathārtham..
vijñātumicchāma yathārthatopi sarve vayaṃ śrotukāmā yayāte.. 15.106 ..
1.3.d:
भूयः पृष्टः सर्वदेवैः स राजा कृतं सर्वं गुप्तमेव यथार्थम्..
विज्ञातुमिच्छाम यथार्थतोपि सर्वे वयं श्रोतुकामा ययाते.. 15.106 ..
1.3.m: The king was questioned again by all the gods: 'Whatever was done secretly, in truth, / we wish to know accurately; we all desire to hear, O Yayāti.' (15.106)

1.3.s:
vaco niśamya devānāṃ yayātiramitadyutiḥ..
kathayāmāsa tatsarvaṃ puṇyaśeṣaṃ yathārthataḥ.. 15.107 ..
1.3.d:
वचो निशम्य देवानां ययातिरमितद्युतिः..
कथयामास तत्सर्वं पुण्यशेषं यथार्थतः.. 15.107 ..
1.3.m: Hearing the words of the gods, Yayāti of boundless splendor / recounted all the remainder of his merit in its true measure. (15.107)

1.3.s:
kathitaṃ sarvametacca niḥśeṣaṃ vyāsavattadā..
svapuṇyakathanenaiva yayātirapatadbhuvi.. 15.108 ..
1.3.d:
कथितं सर्वमेतच्च निःशेषं व्यासवत्तदा..
स्वपुण्यकथनेनैव ययातिरपतद्भुवि.. 15.108 ..
1.3.m: When all this had been told completely, just as Vyāsa [tells it], / Yayāti fell to the earth solely through reciting his own merits. (15.108)

1.3.s:
tatkṣaṇādeva sarveṣāṃ surāṇāṃ tatra paśyatām..
evameva tathā jātamarājakamataṃdritam.. 15.109 ..
1.3.d:
तत्क्षणादेव सर्वेषां सुराणां तत्र पश्यताम्..
एवमेव तथा जातमराजकमतंद्रितम्.. 15.109 ..
1.3.m: At that very moment, before the eyes of all the gods watching there, / the realm became completely kingless, without any protector. (15.109)

1.3.s:
anyo na dṛśyate loke yājñiko yo hi tatra vai..
śakrāsane'bhiṣe kāryaṃ śrūyatāṃ hi dvijottamāḥ.. 15.110 ..
1.3.d:
अन्यो न दृश्यते लोके याज्ञिको यो हि तत्र वै..
शक्रासनेऽभिषे कार्यं श्रूयतां हि द्विजोत्तमाः.. 15.110 ..
1.3.m: 'No other sacrificer is seen in the world who can be consecrated on the throne of Indra'— / listen indeed to this, O best of brahmins! (15.110)

1.3.s:
sarve surāśca ṛṣayo'tha mahāphaṇīṃdrā gandharvayakṣakhagacāraṇakiṃnarāśca..
vidyādharāḥ suragaṇāpsarasāṃ gaṇāśca ciṃtāparāḥ samabhavanmanujāstathaiva.. 15.111 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kedārakhaṇḍe śivaśāstre devendrasvārājyābhiṣekavṛttānte devendrasya brahmahatyayopadrutau nahuṣaśāpayayātibhūṣaṇyavṛttāntavarṇanaṃnāma paṃcadaśo'dhyāyaḥ.. 15 .. cha ..
1.3.d:
सर्वे सुराश्च ऋषयोऽथ महाफणींद्रा गन्धर्वयक्षखगचारणकिंनराश्च..
विद्याधराः सुरगणाप्सरसां गणाश्च चिंतापराः समभवन्मनुजास्तथैव.. 15.111 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे केदारखण्डे शिवशास्त्रे देवेन्द्रस्वाराज्याभिषेकवृत्तान्ते देवेन्द्रस्य ब्रह्महत्ययोपद्रुतौ नहुषशापययातिभूषण्यवृत्तान्तवर्णनंनाम पंचदशोऽध्यायः.. 15 .. छ ..
1.3.m:
All the gods, the seers, the great serpent kings, gandharvas, yakṣas, birds, cāraṇas, and kiṃnaras, / the vidyādharas, the hosts of gods, and the troops of apsarases, as well as mortal men, became filled with anxiety. (15.111)
Thus ends the fifteenth chapter, entitled 'The Description of the Curse of Nahuṣa and the Account of Yayāti's [Fall], in the Story of the Sovereign Consecration of the Lord of Gods, when the Lord of Gods was Beset by the Murder of a Brahmin,' in the treatise on Śiva, within the Kedārakhaṇḍa of the first section, the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, of the glorious Skandamahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses. (15)

1.3.s:
..lomaśa uvāca..
tataḥ śacī tānprovāca vācaṃ dharmārthasaṃyutām..
mā ciṃtā kriyatāṃ devā bṛhaspatipurogamaḥ.. 16.1 ..
1.3.d:
..लोमश उवाच..
ततः शची तान्प्रोवाच वाचं धर्मार्थसंयुताम्..
मा चिंता क्रियतां देवा बृहस्पतिपुरोगमः.. 16.1 ..
1.3.m: Lomaśa said: / Then Śacī addressed them with words full of righteousness and purpose: / 'Do not worry, O gods, with Bṛhaspati at your head! (16.1)

1.3.s:
gacchata tvaritāḥ sarve śakraṃ draṣṭuṃ vicakṣaṇāḥ..
brahmahatyābhibhūto'sau yatrāste surasattamaḥ.. 16.2 ..
1.3.d:
गच्छत त्वरिताः सर्वे शक्रं द्रष्टुं विचक्षणाः..
ब्रह्महत्याभिभूतोऽसौ यत्रास्ते सुरसत्तमः.. 16.2 ..
1.3.m: Go swiftly, all you wise ones, to see Indra, / where that best of gods dwells, overwhelmed by the murder of a brahmin. (16.2)

1.3.s:
bahūnāṃ kāraṇenaiva viśvarūpe hi maṃdadhīḥ..
hatastena maheṃdreṇa sarvaiḥ so'pi nirākṛtaḥ.. 16.3 ..
1.3.d:
बहूनां कारणेनैव विश्वरूपे हि मंदधीः..
हतस्तेन महेंद्रेण सर्वैः सोऽपि निराकृतः.. 16.3 ..
1.3.m: Because Viśvarūpa of dull intellect acted for the sake of many [enemies], / he was slain by that Mahendra, yet he too has been abandoned by all. (16.3)

1.3.s:
tasmātsarvairbhavadbhiśca gaṃtavyaṃ yatra sa prabhuḥ..
avajñā hi kṛtā pūrvaṃ maheṃdreṇa tavānagha.. 16.4 ..
1.3.d:
तस्मात्सर्वैर्भवद्भिश्च गंतव्यं यत्र स प्रभुः..
अवज्ञा हि कृता पूर्वं महेंद्रेण तवानघ.. 16.4 ..
1.3.m: Therefore, all of you must go where that lord is. / For formerly, O sinless one, Indra showed disrespect toward you. (16.4)

1.3.s:
avajñāmātrakṣubaṃdhena tvayā śaptaḥ puraṃdaraḥ..
tathaiva śāpitaścāsi mayā tvaṃ hi bṛhaspate.. 16.5 ..
1.3.d:
अवज्ञामात्रक्षुबंधेन त्वया शप्तः पुरंदरः..
तथैव शापितश्चासि मया त्वं हि बृहस्पते.. 16.5 ..
1.3.m: Bound by the mere agitation of that disrespect, Indra was cursed by you, / and in that very way, O Bṛhaspati, you too were cursed by me. (16.5)

1.3.s: nirasto'pi hi tasmāttvamavasānaparo bhava.. 16.6 ..
1.3.d: निरस्तोऽपि हि तस्मात्त्वमवसानपरो भव.. 16.6 ..
1.3.m: Although dismissed from that [station], do you now bring an end [to this misfortune]. (16.6)

1.3.s:
yathā madarthamānītau śakre jīvati tāvubhau..
tvayi jīvati bho brahamankāryaṃ tava kariṣyati.. 16.7 ..
1.3.d:
यथा मदर्थमानीतौ शक्रे जीवति तावुभौ..
त्वयि जीवति भो ब्रहमन्कार्यं तव करिष्यति.. 16.7 ..
1.3.m: Just as both of those [kings] were brought for my sake while Indra was alive, / so, while you are alive, O brahmin, who will do your work? (16.7)

1.3.s:
ko'pi saubhāgyavām̐lloke tava kṣetre janiṣyati..
putraṃ vikhyātanāmānamatranaivāsti saṃśayaḥ.. 16.8 ..
1.3.d:
कोऽपि सौभाग्यवाम्̐ल्लोके तव क्षेत्रे जनिष्यति..
पुत्रं विख्यातनामानमत्रनैवास्ति संशयः.. 16.8 ..
1.3.m: A fortunate one shall be born in your lineage in this world, / a son of renowned name; of this there is no doubt. (16.8)

1.3.s:
gaccha śīghraṃ suraiḥsārddhaṃ śakramānaya ma ciram..
prayāsi tvarito no cetpunaḥ śāpaṃ dadāmi te.. 16.9 ..
1.3.d:
गच्छ शीघ्रं सुरैःसार्द्धं शक्रमानय म चिरम्..
प्रयासि त्वरितो नो चेत्पुनः शापं ददामि ते.. 16.9 ..
1.3.m: Go quickly with the gods; bring Indra without delay. / If you do not depart at once, I will curse you again.' (16.9)

1.3.s:
śacyoktaṃ vacanaṃ śrutvā suraiḥ sārddhaṃ jagāma saḥ..
puraṃdaraṃ gatāḥ sarve brahmahatyābhipīḍitam.. 16.10 ..
1.3.d:
शच्योक्तं वचनं श्रुत्वा सुरैः सार्द्धं जगाम सः..
पुरंदरं गताः सर्वे ब्रह्महत्याभिपीडितम्.. 16.10 ..
1.3.m: Hearing the speech uttered by Śacī, he set out along with the gods. / They all went to Purandara, who was afflicted by the murder of a brahmin. (16.10)

1.3.s:
sarasastīramāsādya te śakraṃ cābhyavādayan..
dṛṣṭāḥ śakrema te sarve tadā hyapsu sthitena vai.. 16.11 ..
1.3.d:
सरसस्तीरमासाद्य ते शक्रं चाभ्यवादयन्..
दृष्टाः शक्रेम ते सर्वे तदा ह्यप्सु स्थितेन वै.. 16.11 ..
1.3.m: Reaching the shore of a lake, they saluted Indra; / and they were all seen by Indra, who was then dwelling in the waters. (16.11)

1.3.s:
uvāca devānedeveśaḥ kasmādyūyamihāgatāḥ..
ahaṃ hi pātakagrasto brahmahatyāparipsutaḥ..
apsu tiṣṭhāmi bho devā ekākī tapasānvitaḥ.. 16.12 ..
1.3.d:
उवाच देवानेदेवेशः कस्माद्यूयमिहागताः..
अहं हि पातकग्रस्तो ब्रह्महत्यापरिप्सुतः..
अप्सु तिष्ठामि भो देवा एकाकी तपसान्वितः.. 16.12 ..
1.3.m: The lord of the gods said to the gods: 'Why have you come here? / Seized by wickedness and pursued by the murder of a brahmin, / I dwell in the waters, O gods, alone and engaged in austerity.' (16.12)

1.3.s:
tacchrutvā vacanaṃ tasya sarve devāḥ śatakratoḥ..
ūcurvihvalitā enaṃ devarājānamadbhutam.. 16.13 ..
1.3.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा वचनं तस्य सर्वे देवाः शतक्रतोः..
ऊचुर्विह्वलिता एनं देवराजानमद्भुतम्.. 16.13 ..
1.3.m: Hearing those words of his, all the gods of Śatakratu, / distressed, addressed this wonderful king of the gods: (16.13)

1.3.s:
etādṛśaṃ na vācyaṃ te pareṣāmupakārataḥ..
kṛtaṃ tvayaiva yatkarma viśvarūpavadhādikam.. 16.14 ..
1.3.d:
एतादृशं न वाच्यं ते परेषामुपकारतः..
कृतं त्वयैव यत्कर्म विश्वरूपवधादिकम्.. 16.14 ..
1.3.m: 'Such a thing should not be spoken by you. It was for the benefit of others / that that deed—the slaying of Viśvarūpa and the rest—was performed by you. (16.14)

1.3.s:
viśvakarmasutenaiva kṛtaṃ yājanamadbhutam..
yena devāḥ kṣayaṃ yāṃti ṛṣayo'pi mahāprabhāḥ.. 16.15 ..
1.3.d:
विश्वकर्मसुतेनैव कृतं याजनमद्भुतम्..
येन देवाः क्षयं यांति ऋषयोऽपि महाप्रभाः.. 16.15 ..
1.3.m: A wondrous sacrifice was performed by the son of Viśvakarman, / through which the gods, and even the seers of great splendor, were perishing. (16.15)

1.3.s:
tasmādvatastvayā deva pareṣāmupakārataḥ..
tataḥ sarve vayaṃ prāptāstvāṃ netumamarāvatīm.. 16.16 ..
1.3.d:
तस्माद्वतस्त्वया देव परेषामुपकारतः..
ततः सर्वे वयं प्राप्तास्त्वां नेतुममरावतीम्.. 16.16 ..
1.3.m: Therefore he was slain by you, O lord, for the benefit of others; / hence we have all arrived to take you back to Amarāvatī.' (16.16)

1.3.s:
evaṃ vivadamāneṣu deveṣu ca tadā'bravīt..
brahmahatyā tvarāyuktā deveṃdraṃ varayāmyaham.. 16.17 ..
1.3.d:
एवं विवदमानेषु देवेषु च तदाऽब्रवीत्..
ब्रह्महत्या त्वरायुक्ता देवेंद्रं वरयाम्यहम्.. 16.17 ..
1.3.m: While the gods were disputing thus, [the personified] Murder of a Brahmin / spoke in haste: 'I choose the lord of gods!' (16.17)

1.3.s: tadā bṛhaspatirvākyamuvāca sahasaiva tu.. 16.18 ..
1.3.d: तदा बृहस्पतिर्वाक्यमुवाच सहसैव तु.. 16.18 ..
1.3.m: Then Bṛhaspati at once spoke words [to her]: (16.18)

1.3.s:
..bṛhaspatiruvāca..
vāsārthaṃ ca kariṣyāmaḥ sthānāni tava sāṃpratam..
prasāṃtvitā tadā hatyā devaistatkāryagauravāt.. 16.19 ..
1.3.d:
..बृहस्पतिरुवाच..
वासार्थं च करिष्यामः स्थानानि तव सांप्रतम्..
प्रसांत्विता तदा हत्या देवैस्तत्कार्यगौरवात्.. 16.19 ..
1.3.m: Bṛhaspati said: / 'We shall now prepare places for your dwelling.' / The [sin of] murder was then pacified by the gods because of the gravity of that task. (16.19)

1.3.s:
vimṛśya sarve vibhajuścaturddhā hatyāṃ surāste ṛṣayo manīṣiṇaḥ..
yakṣāḥ piśācā uragāḥ pataṃgāstathā ca sarve surasiddhacāraṇāḥ.. 16.20 ..
1.3.d:
विमृश्य सर्वे विभजुश्चतुर्द्धा हत्यां सुरास्ते ऋषयो मनीषिणः..
यक्षाः पिशाचा उरगाः पतंगास्तथा च सर्वे सुरसिद्धचारणाः.. 16.20 ..
1.3.m: Reflecting, those gods, wise seers, / yakṣas, piśācas, serpents, birds, and all the deities, siddhas, and cāraṇas divided the sin of murder into four parts. (16.20)

1.3.s:
ādau kṣamāṃ prati tadā ūcuḥ sarve divaukasaḥ..
he kṣameṃ'śastvayā grāhyo hatyāyāḥ kāryasiddhaye.. 16.21 ..
1.3.d:
आदौ क्षमां प्रति तदा ऊचुः सर्वे दिवौकसः..
हे क्षमेंऽशस्त्वया ग्राह्यो हत्यायाः कार्यसिद्धये.. 16.21 ..
1.3.m: At first, all the celestials addressed the Earth: / 'O Earth, a share of this murder must be accepted by you for the accomplishment of this purpose.' (16.21)

1.3.s:
surāṇāṃ tadvacaḥ śrutvā dharitrī kaṃpitā'vadat..
kathaṃ grāhye mayā hyaṃśo hatyāyāstadvimṛśyatām.. 16.22 ..
1.3.d:
सुराणां तद्वचः श्रुत्वा धरित्री कंपिताऽवदत्..
कथं ग्राह्ये मया ह्यंशो हत्यायास्तद्विमृश्यताम्.. 16.22 ..
1.3.m: Hearing those words of the gods, the Earth trembled and said: / 'How should a portion of this murder be taken by me? Consider that! (16.22)

1.3.s:
ahaṃ hi sarvabhūtānāṃ dhātrī viśvaṃ dharāmyaham..
apavitrā bhaviṣyāmi enasā saṃvṛtā bhṛśam.. 16.23 ..
1.3.d:
अहं हि सर्वभूतानां धात्री विश्वं धराम्यहम्..
अपवित्रा भविष्यामि एनसा संवृता भृशम्.. 16.23 ..
1.3.m: I am indeed the supporter of all beings; I uphold the universe. / Covered intensely by this sin, I shall become impure.' (16.23)

1.3.s:
pṛthvayāstadvacanaṃ śrutvā bṛhaspatiruvāca tām..
mā bhauṣīścārusarvāṃgi niṣpāpāsi na cānyathā.. 16.24 ..
1.3.d:
पृथ्वयास्तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा बृहस्पतिरुवाच ताम्..
मा भौषीश्चारुसर्वांगि निष्पापासि न चान्यथा.. 16.24 ..
1.3.m: Hearing that speech of the Earth, Bṛhaspati said to her: / 'Do not fear, O fair-limbed one! You will be sinless, not otherwise. (16.24)

1.3.s:
yadā yadukule śrīmānvāsudevo bhaviṣyati..
tadā tatpadavinyāsānnaṣpāpā tvaṃ bhaviṣyasi.. 16.25 ..
1.3.d:
यदा यदुकुले श्रीमान्वासुदेवो भविष्यति..
तदा तत्पदविन्यासान्नष्पापा त्वं भविष्यसि.. 16.25 ..
1.3.m: When the glorious Vāsudeva appears in the lineage of the Yadus, / you shall become sinless through the imprint of his footsteps. (16.25)

1.3.s: kuru vākyaṃ tvamasmākaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā.. 16.26 ..
1.3.d: कुरु वाक्यं त्वमस्माकं नात्र कार्या विचारणा.. 16.26 ..
1.3.m: Heed our words; there should be no hesitation here.' (16.26)

1.3.s:
ityuktā pṛthivī teṣāṃ niṣpāpā sākarodvacaḥ..
tato vṛkṣānsamāhūya sarve devā'bruvanvacaḥ.. 16.27 ..
1.3.d:
इत्युक्ता पृथिवी तेषां निष्पापा साकरोद्वचः..
ततो वृक्षान्समाहूय सर्वे देवाऽब्रुवन्वचः.. 16.27 ..
1.3.m: Thus addressed, the Earth, [assured of being] free from sin, obeyed their command. / Then, summoning the trees, all the gods spoke these words: (16.27)

1.3.s:
hatyāṃśo hi grahītavyo bhavadbhiḥ kāryasiddhaye..
evamuktā'bruvanvabṛkṣā devānsarve samāgatāḥ.. 16.28 ..
1.3.d:
हत्यांशो हि ग्रहीतव्यो भवद्भिः कार्यसिद्धये..
एवमुक्ताऽब्रुवन्वबृक्षा देवान्सर्वे समागताः.. 16.28 ..
1.3.m: 'A portion of this murder must be accepted by you for the accomplishment of our purpose.' / Thus addressed, all the assembled trees said to the gods: (16.28)

1.3.s:
vayaṃ sarve tathā bhūtāstāpasānāṃ phalapradāḥ..
tadā hatyānvitāḥ sarve bhaviṣyaṃti tapasvinaḥ.. 16.29 ..
1.3.d:
वयं सर्वे तथा भूतास्तापसानां फलप्रदाः..
तदा हत्यान्विताः सर्वे भविष्यंति तपस्विनः.. 16.29 ..
1.3.m: 'We all exist in such a way as to provide fruits to ascetics; / then all those performers of austerity will become infected with the sin of murder, (16.29)

1.3.s:
pāpino hi mahābhāgāstasmātsarvaṃ vimṛśyatām..
tadā purodhasā coktāḥ sarve vṛkṣāḥ samāgatāḥ.. 16.30 ..
1.3.d:
पापिनो हि महाभागास्तस्मात्सर्वं विमृश्यताम्..
तदा पुरोधसा चोक्ताः सर्वे वृक्षाः समागताः.. 16.30 ..
1.3.m: becoming sinners, O fortunate ones; therefore consider everything!' / Then all the assembled trees were addressed by the family priest: (16.30)

1.3.s:
mā ciṃtā kriyatāṃ sarvaiḥ prasādācca śatakratoḥ..
cheditāścaiva sarve vai hyanekāṃśatvamāgatāḥ.. 16.31 ..
1.3.d:
मा चिंता क्रियतां सर्वैः प्रसादाच्च शतक्रतोः..
छेदिताश्चैव सर्वे वै ह्यनेकांशत्वमागताः.. 16.31 ..
1.3.m: "Let no worry be had by all of you; by the grace of Śatakratu, / even when cut down, all of you will attain manifold branches.

1.3.s:
tato viṭapino nityaṃ yūyaṃ sarve bhaviṣyatha..
ityuktāste tadā sarvegṛhṇanhatyāṃ vibhāgaśaḥ.. 16.32 ..
1.3.d:
ततो विटपिनो नित्यं यूयं सर्वे भविष्यथ..
इत्युक्तास्ते तदा सर्वेगृह्णन्हत्यां विभागशः.. 16.32 ..
1.3.m: From that you will all continually be trees with branches." / Being addressed thus, all of them then took the guilt of murder in parts.

1.3.s:
tato hyapaḥ samāhūya ūcuḥ sarve divaukasaḥ..
adbhiśca gṛhyatāmadya hatyāṃśaḥ kāryasiddhaye.. 16.33 ..
1.3.d:
ततो ह्यपः समाहूय ऊचुः सर्वे दिवौकसः..
अद्भिश्च गृह्यतामद्य हत्यांशः कार्यसिद्धये.. 16.33 ..
1.3.m: Then, summoning the waters, all the sky-dwellers said: / "Let a portion of the guilt of murder be taken today by the waters for the accomplishment of our purpose."

1.3.s:
tadā hyāpo militvātha ūcuḥ sarvāḥ purodhasam..
yāni kāni ca pāpāni tathā duścaritāni ca.. 16.34 ..
1.3.d:
तदा ह्यापो मिलित्वाथ ऊचुः सर्वाः पुरोधसम्..
यानि कानि च पापानि तथा दुश्चरितानि च.. 16.34 ..
1.3.m: Then indeed the waters, assembling together, spoke to the priest: / "Whatever sins and wicked deeds there are,

1.3.s:
asmatsaṃparkasaṃbaṃdhātsnānaśaucāśanādibhiḥ..
punaṃti prāṇinaḥ sarve pāpena pariveṣṭitāḥ.. 16.35 ..
1.3.d:
अस्मत्संपर्कसंबंधात्स्नानशौचाशनादिभिः..
पुनंति प्राणिनः सर्वे पापेन परिवेष्टिताः.. 16.35 ..
1.3.m: through contact and connection with us, by bathing, washing, drinking, and the like, / all living beings encircled by sin become purified.

1.3.s:
tāsāṃ vacanamākarṇya bṛhaspatiruvāca ha..
mā bhayaṃ kriyatāmāpa enasā dustareṇa hi.. 16.36 ..
1.3.d:
तासां वचनमाकर्ण्य बृहस्पतिरुवाच ह..
मा भयं क्रियतामाप एनसा दुस्तरेण हि.. 16.36 ..
1.3.m: Hearing their words, Bṛhaspati said: / "Let no fear be had, O waters, of this sin that is hard to cross!

1.3.s:
āpaḥ punaṃtu sarveṣāṃ carācaranivāsinām..
tadā striyaḥ samāhūya bṛhaspatiruvāca ha.. 16.37 ..
1.3.d:
आपः पुनंतु सर्वेषां चराचरनिवासिनाम्..
तदा स्त्रियः समाहूय बृहस्पतिरुवाच ह.. 16.37 ..
1.3.m: May the waters purify all the dwellers among the moving and unmoving!" / Then, summoning women, Bṛhaspati said:

1.3.s:
adyaiva grāhye hatyāṃśaḥ sarvakāryārthasiddhaye..
niśamya tadgurorvākyamūcuḥ sarvāścayopitaḥ.. 16.38 ..
1.3.d:
अद्यैव ग्राह्ये हत्यांशः सर्वकार्यार्थसिद्धये..
निशम्य तद्गुरोर्वाक्यमूचुः सर्वाश्चयोपितः.. 16.38 ..
1.3.m: "Today itself a portion of the guilt of murder should be accepted for the sake of accomplishing all tasks." / Hearing that word of their guru, all the women spoke:

1.3.s:
pāpamācarate yoṣā tena pāpena nānyathā..
lipyaṃte bahavaḥ pakṣā iti vedānuśāsanam.. 16.39 ..
1.3.d:
पापमाचरते योषा तेन पापेन नान्यथा..
लिप्यंते बहवः पक्षा इति वेदानुशासनम्.. 16.39 ..
1.3.m: "If a woman commits a sin, by that sin / many parties are tainted, and not otherwise—such is the Vedic ordinance.

1.3.s:
śrutamasti na te kiṃciddhepurodho vimṛśyatām..
yoṣidbhiḥ procyamāno'pi uvācātha bṛhaspatiḥ.. 16.40 ..
1.3.d:
श्रुतमस्ति न ते किंचिद्धेपुरोधो विमृश्यताम्..
योषिद्भिः प्रोच्यमानोऽपि उवाचाथ बृहस्पतिः.. 16.40 ..
1.3.m: Have you not heard anything, O priest? Reflect upon it!" / Though being spoken to thus by the women, Bṛhaspati then said:

1.3.s:
mā bhayaṃ kriyatāṃ sarvāḥ pāpādasmātsulocanāḥ..
bhaviṣyāṇāṃ tathānyeṣāṃ bhaviṣyati phalapradaḥ..
hatyāṃśo yo hi sarvāsāṃ yathākāmitvameva ca.. 16.41 ..
1.3.d:
मा भयं क्रियतां सर्वाः पापादस्मात्सुलोचनाः..
भविष्याणां तथान्येषां भविष्यति फलप्रदः..
हत्यांशो यो हि सर्वासां यथाकामित्वमेव च.. 16.41 ..
1.3.m: "Let no fear be had from this sin by all of you, fair-eyed ones! / It will bear fruit for those [children] to be born and for others; / whatever portion of the guilt of murder belongs to all of you, you shall act according to your desire."

1.3.s:
evamaṃśāśca tyāyāścatvāraḥ kalpitāḥ suraiḥ..
nivāsamakarotsadyasteṣuteṣu dvijottamāḥ.. 16.42 ..
1.3.d:
एवमंशाश्च त्यायाश्चत्वारः कल्पिताः सुरैः..
निवासमकरोत्सद्यस्तेषुतेषु द्विजोत्तमाः.. 16.42 ..
1.3.m: Thus four portions of the guilt of murder were arranged by the gods; / it immediately took up residence in those several [entities], O best of brahmins.

1.3.s:
niṣpāpo hi tadā jāto maheṃdro hyabhiṣecitaḥ..
devapuryāṃ suragaṇaistathaiva ṛṣabhiḥ saha.. 16.43 ..
1.3.d:
निष्पापो हि तदा जातो महेंद्रो ह्यभिषेचितः..
देवपुर्यां सुरगणैस्तथैव ऋषभिः सह.. 16.43 ..
1.3.m: Then Mahendra became free of sin and was consecrated / in the city of the gods by the hosts of gods and also with the seers.

1.3.s:
śacyā sameto hi tadā puraṃdaro babhūva viśvādhipatirmahātmā..
devaiḥ sameto hi mahānubhāvairmunīśvaraiḥ siddhagaṇaistadānīm.. 16.44 ..
1.3.d:
शच्या समेतो हि तदा पुरंदरो बभूव विश्वाधिपतिर्महात्मा..
देवैः समेतो हि महानुभावैर्मुनीश्वरैः सिद्धगणैस्तदानीम्.. 16.44 ..
1.3.m: Then Puraṃdara, together with Śacī, became the great-souled ruler of the universe, / accompanied at that time by the gods of great dignity, the lords of sages, and the hosts of siddhas.

1.3.s:
tadāgnayaḥ śobhanā vāyavaśca sarve grahāḥ suprabhāḥ śāṃtiyuktāḥ..
jātāḥ sadyaḥ pṛthivī śobhamānā tathādrayo maṇiprabhavā babhūvuḥ.. 16.45 ..
1.3.d:
तदाग्नयः शोभना वायवश्च सर्वे ग्रहाः सुप्रभाः शांतियुक्ताः..
जाताः सद्यः पृथिवी शोभमाना तथाद्रयो मणिप्रभवा बभूवुः.. 16.45 ..
1.3.m: Then the fires became radiant, the winds [pleasant], and all planets brightly shining and peaceful; / the earth immediately became beauteous, and the mountains became sources of gems.

1.3.s: prasannāni tathā hyāsanmanāṃsi ca manasvinām.. 16.46 ..
1.3.d: प्रसन्नानि तथा ह्यासन्मनांसि च मनस्विनाम्.. 16.46 ..
1.3.m: And the minds of the wise became serene.

1.3.s:
nadyaścāmṛtavāhinyo vṛkṣā hyāsansadāphalāḥ..
akṛṣṭapacyauṣadhayo babhūvuścamṛtopamāḥ.. 16.47 ..
1.3.d:
नद्यश्चामृतवाहिन्यो वृक्षा ह्यासन्सदाफलाः..
अकृष्टपच्यौषधयो बभूवुश्चमृतोपमाः.. 16.47 ..
1.3.m: The rivers flowed with nectar; the trees bore fruit continually; / the plants ripened without cultivation and became like nectar.

1.3.s:
aikapadyena sarveṣāmiṃdralokanivāsinām..
babhūva paramotsāho mahāmodakarastathā.. 16.48 ..
1.3.d:
ऐकपद्येन सर्वेषामिंद्रलोकनिवासिनाम्..
बभूव परमोत्साहो महामोदकरस्तथा.. 16.48 ..
1.3.m: For all the dwellers of Indra's world, in unison, / there arose supreme enthusiasm that produced great joy.

1.3.s:
..lomaśa uvāca..
etasminnaṃtare tvaṣṭā dṛṣṭvā ceṃdramahotsavam..
babhūva ruṣi to'tīva putraśokaprapīḍitaḥ.. 16.49 ..
1.3.d:
..लोमश उवाच..
एतस्मिन्नंतरे त्वष्टा दृष्ट्वा चेंद्रमहोत्सवम्..
बभूव रुषि तोऽतीव पुत्रशोकप्रपीडितः.. 16.49 ..
1.3.m: Lomaśa said: / In the meantime Tvaṣṭṛ, seeing the great festival of Indra, / became exceedingly enraged, tormented by grief for his son.

1.3.s:
jagāma nirvedaparastapastaptuṃ sudāruṇam..
tapasā tena saṃtuṣṭo brahmā lokapitāmahaḥ.. 16.50 ..
1.3.d:
जगाम निर्वेदपरस्तपस्तप्तुं सुदारुणम्..
तपसा तेन संतुष्टो ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः.. 16.50 ..
1.3.m: Overcome by dejection, he went to perform very terrible austerity. / Pleased by that austerity, Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds,

1.3.s:
tvaṣṭāramabravīttuṣṭo varaṃ varaya suvrata..
tadā vavre varaṃ tvaṣṭā sarvalokabhayāvaham..
varaṃ putro hi dātvoya devānāṃ hi bhayāvahaḥ.. 16.51 ..
1.3.d:
त्वष्टारमब्रवीत्तुष्टो वरं वरय सुव्रत..
तदा वव्रे वरं त्वष्टा सर्वलोकभयावहम्..
वरं पुत्रो हि दात्वोय देवानां हि भयावहः.. 16.51 ..
1.3.m: pleased, said to Tvaṣṭṛ: "Choose a boon, O one of good vows!" / Then Tvaṣṭṛ chose a boon that struck terror into all the worlds: / "A boon: let a son be given who will strike fear into the gods!"

1.3.s:
tatheti ca varo datto brahmaṇā parameṣṭhinā..
varadānātsadya eva babhūva puruṣastadā.. 16.52 ..
1.3.d:
तथेति च वरो दत्तो ब्रह्मणा परमेष्ठिना..
वरदानात्सद्य एव बभूव पुरुषस्तदा.. 16.52 ..
1.3.m: "So be it," and thus the boon was granted by Brahmā Parameṣṭhin. / From the granting of the boon, a man immediately appeared at that time,

1.3.s:
vṛtranāmāṃkitastatra daityo hi paramādbhutaḥ..
dhanuṣāṃ śatamātraṃ hi pratyahaṃ vavṛdhe'suraḥ.. 16.53 ..
1.3.d:
वृत्रनामांकितस्तत्र दैत्यो हि परमाद्भुतः..
धनुषां शतमात्रं हि प्रत्यहं ववृधेऽसुरः.. 16.53 ..
1.3.m: marked with the name Vṛtra, a daitya of supreme wonder. / That asura grew daily by a measure of a hundred bows.

1.3.s:
pātālānnirgatā daityā ye purā'mṛtamaṃthane..
ghātitāḥ surasaṃghaiśca bhṛguṇā jīvitāstvarāt.. 16.54 ..
1.3.d:
पातालान्निर्गता दैत्या ये पुराऽमृतमंथने..
घातिताः सुरसंघैश्च भृगुणा जीवितास्त्वरात्.. 16.54 ..
1.3.m: From Pātāla emerged the daityas who formerly, during the churning of the nectar, / had been slain by the hosts of gods and were quickly revived by Bhṛgu.

1.3.s: sarvaṃ mahītalaṃ vyāptaṃ tenaikena mahātmanā.. 16.55 ..
1.3.d: सर्वं महीतलं व्याप्तं तेनैकेन महात्मना.. 16.55 ..
1.3.m: The whole surface of the earth was pervaded by that single great-souled one.

1.3.s:
tadā sarve'pi ṛṣayo vadhyamānāstapasvinaḥ..
brahmāṇaṃ tvaritāḥ sarve ūcurvyasanamāgatam.. 16.56 ..
1.3.d:
तदा सर्वेऽपि ऋषयो वध्यमानास्तपस्विनः..
ब्रह्माणं त्वरिताः सर्वे ऊचुर्व्यसनमागतम्.. 16.56 ..
1.3.m: Then all the seers, ascetics being slain, / quickly approached Brahmā and spoke of the calamity that had arrived,

1.3.s:
tathā ceṃdrādayo devā gaṃdharvāḥ samarudgaṇāḥ..
brahmaṇā kathitaṃ sarvaṃ tvaṣṭuścaitaccikīrṣitam.. 16.57 ..
1.3.d:
तथा चेंद्रादयो देवा गंधर्वाः समरुद्गणाः..
ब्रह्मणा कथितं सर्वं त्वष्टुश्चैतच्चिकीर्षितम्.. 16.57 ..
1.3.m: as did the gods led by Indra, the gandharvas, along with the hosts of Maruts. / Brahmā narrated everything—this undertaking of Tvaṣṭṛ:

1.3.s:
bhavadvadhārthaṃ janitastapasā parameṇa tu..
vṛttronāma mahātejāḥ sarvadaityāpidho mahān.. 16.58 ..
1.3.d:
भवद्वधार्थं जनितस्तपसा परमेण तु..
वृत्त्रोनाम महातेजाः सर्वदैत्यापिधो महान्.. 16.58 ..
1.3.m: "For the sake of your death he has been generated by supreme austerity, / great in splendour, named Vṛtra, covering all the daityas, a great one.

1.3.s:
tathāpi yatnaḥ kriyatāṃ yathā vadhyo bhavedasau..
niśamya brahmaṇo vākyamūcurddevāḥ savāsavāḥ.. 16.59 ..
1.3.d:
तथापि यत्नः क्रियतां यथा वध्यो भवेदसौ..
निशम्य ब्रह्मणो वाक्यमूचुर्द्देवाः सवासवाः.. 16.59 ..
1.3.m: Nevertheless, make an effort so that he may be killed." / Hearing the word of Brahmā, the gods along with Indra spoke.

1.3.s:
.. devā ūcuḥ..
yadā iṃdro hi hatyāyā vimuktaḥ sthāpito divi..
tadāsmābhirakāryaṃ vai kṛtamasti durāsadam.. 16.60 ..
1.3.d:
.. देवा ऊचुः..
यदा इंद्रो हि हत्याया विमुक्तः स्थापितो दिवि..
तदास्माभिरकार्यं वै कृतमस्ति दुरासदम्.. 16.60 ..
1.3.m: The gods said: / "When Indra was freed from the guilt of murder and established in heaven, / then an improper deed, hard to endure, was done by us.

1.3.s:
śastrāṇyastrāṇyanekāni saṃkṣiptāni hyabuddhitaḥ..
dadhīca syāśrame brahmankiṃ kāryaṃ karavāmahe.. 16.61 ..
1.3.d:
शस्त्राण्यस्त्राण्यनेकानि संक्षिप्तानि ह्यबुद्धितः..
दधीच स्याश्रमे ब्रह्मन्किं कार्यं करवामहे.. 16.61 ..
1.3.m: Many weapons and missiles were deposited thoughtlessly / in the hermitage of Dadhīca, O Brahmā; what duty shall we perform?"

1.3.s:
tacchrutvā prahasanvākyaṃ devānbrahmā tadā'bravīt..
ciraṃ sthitāni vijñāyāgacchadhvaṃ tāni vai surāḥ.. 16.62 ..
1.3.d:
तच्छ्रुत्वा प्रहसन्वाक्यं देवान्ब्रह्मा तदाऽब्रवीत्..
चिरं स्थितानि विज्ञायागच्छध्वं तानि वै सुराः.. 16.62 ..
1.3.m: Hearing that statement, Brahmā, laughing, said to the gods: / "Go, knowing that they have remained there for a long time, O gods!"

1.3.s:
gatvā devāstadā sarve nāpaśyansvaṃ svamāyudham..
papracchuśca dadhīciṃ te so'vādīnnaiva vedbhayaham.. 16.63 ..
1.3.d:
गत्वा देवास्तदा सर्वे नापश्यन्स्वं स्वमायुधम्..
पप्रच्छुश्च दधीचिं ते सोऽवादीन्नैव वेद्भयहम्.. 16.63 ..
1.3.m: All the gods, having gone then, did not see their respective weapons. / And they questioned Dadhīci; he spoke: "I truly do not know."

1.3.s: punarbrahmāṇamāgātya ūcuḥ sarve munervacaḥ.. 16.64 ..
1.3.d: पुनर्ब्रह्माणमागात्य ऊचुः सर्वे मुनेर्वचः.. 16.64 ..
1.3.m: Coming again to Brahmā, they all related the words of the sage.

1.3.s:
brahmovāca tadā devānsarveṣāṃ kāryasiddhaye..
tasyāsthīnyeva yācadhvaṃ pradāsyati na saṃśayaḥ.. 16.65 ..
1.3.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच तदा देवान्सर्वेषां कार्यसिद्धये..
तस्यास्थीन्येव याचध्वं प्रदास्यति न संशयः.. 16.65 ..
1.3.m: Brahmā then said to the gods for the accomplishment of everyone's purpose: / "Beg for his very bones; he will give them, there is no doubt."

1.3.s: tacchrutvā brāhmaṇo vākyaṃ śakro vacanamabravīt.. 16.66 ..
1.3.d: तच्छ्रुत्वा ब्राह्मणो वाक्यं शक्रो वचनमब्रवीत्.. 16.66 ..
1.3.m: Hearing that word of Brahmā, Śakra spoke these words:

1.3.s:
viśvarūpo hato deva devānāṃ kāryasiddhaye..
eka eva tadā brahmanpāpiṣṭho'haṃ kṛtaḥ suraiḥ.. 16.67 ..
1.3.d:
विश्वरूपो हतो देव देवानां कार्यसिद्धये..
एक एव तदा ब्रह्मन्पापिष्ठोऽहं कृतः सुरैः.. 16.67 ..
1.3.m: "Viśvarūpa was slain, O god, for the accomplishment of the purpose of the gods; / yet then I alone, O Brahmā, was made the most sinful one by the gods,

1.3.s:
tathā purodhasā caiva niḥśrīkastatkṣaṇātkṛtaḥ..
diṣṭyā paramayā cāhaṃ praviṣṭo nijamaṃdiram.. 16.68 ..
1.3.d:
तथा पुरोधसा चैव निःश्रीकस्तत्क्षणात्कृतः..
दिष्ट्या परमया चाहं प्रविष्टो निजमंदिरम्.. 16.68 ..
1.3.m: and also made devoid of majesty in an instant by the priest; / and by supreme good fortune I entered my own abode.

1.3.s:
dadhīcaṃ ghātayitvā vai tasyāsthīni bahūnyapi..
astrāṇi tāni bhagavankṛtāni hyaśubhāni vai.. 16.69 ..
1.3.d:
दधीचं घातयित्वा वै तस्यास्थीनि बहून्यपि..
अस्त्राणि तानि भगवन्कृतानि ह्यशुभानि वै.. 16.69 ..
1.3.m: Having caused Dadhīca to be killed, his many bones / have been turned into weapons, O Lord, and truly inauspicious ones!

1.3.s:
tvaṣṭrā hi janito yo vai vṛtro nāmaiṣa daityarāṭ..
kathaṃ taṃ ghātayāmyevaṃ satataṃ pāpabhīruṇā..
śakreṇoktaṃ niśamyātha brahmā vākyamuvāca ha.. 16.70 ..
1.3.d:
त्वष्ट्रा हि जनितो यो वै वृत्रो नामैष दैत्यराट्..
कथं तं घातयाम्येवं सततं पापभीरुणा..
शक्रेणोक्तं निशम्याथ ब्रह्मा वाक्यमुवाच ह.. 16.70 ..
1.3.m: How can I kill this king of daityas, named Vṛtra, who was generated by Tvaṣṭṛ? / Thus, hearing Śakra, who was constantly afraid of sin, / Brahmā then spoke these words;

1.3.s:
arthaśāstrapareṇaiva vidhinā tamabodhayat..
ātatāyinamāyāṃtaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vā tapasvinam..
haṃtukāmaṃ jighāṃsīyānna tena brahmahā bhavet.. 16.71 ..
1.3.d:
अर्थशास्त्रपरेणैव विधिना तमबोधयत्..
आततायिनमायांतं ब्राह्मणं वा तपस्विनम्..
हंतुकामं जिघांसीयान्न तेन ब्रह्महा भवेत्.. 16.71 ..
1.3.m: he instructed him by the rule pertaining to statecraft alone: / "If an assailant, even a brahmin or an ascetic, approaches / wishing to kill, one should wish to kill him; thereby one does not become the slayer of a brahmin."

1.3.s:
..indra uvāca..
dadhīcasya vadhādbrahmannahaṃ bhīto na saṃśayaḥ..
tasmādbrahmavadhātsatyaṃ mahadeno bhaviṣyati.. 16.72 ..
1.3.d:
..इन्द्र उवाच..
दधीचस्य वधाद्ब्रह्मन्नहं भीतो न संशयः..
तस्माद्ब्रह्मवधात्सत्यं महदेनो भविष्यति.. 16.72 ..
1.3.m: Indra said: / "I am afraid of the killing of Dadhīca, O Brahmā, there is no doubt; / from that slaying of a brahmin, truly a great sin will arise.

1.3.s:
ato na kāryamasmābhirbrāhmaṇānāṃ tu helanam..
helanādbahavo doṣā bhaviṣyaṃti na cānyathā.. 16.73 ..
1.3.d:
अतो न कार्यमस्माभिर्ब्राह्मणानां तु हेलनम्..
हेलनाद्बहवो दोषा भविष्यंति न चान्यथा.. 16.73 ..
1.3.m: Therefore, disrespect toward brahmins must not be done by us; / from disrespect many evils will arise, and not otherwise."

1.3.s:
adṛṣṭaṃ paramaṃ dharmyaṃ vidhinā parameṇa hi..
kartavyaṃ manasā caivaṃ puruṣeṇa vijānatā.. 16.74 ..
1.3.d:
अदृष्टं परमं धर्म्यं विधिना परमेण हि..
कर्तव्यं मनसा चैवं पुरुषेण विजानता.. 16.74 ..
1.3.m: The unseen, supreme merit / must indeed be performed by an understanding man, with highest order and mindful thought. 16.74

1.3.s:
niḥspṛhaṃ tasya tadvākyaṃ śrutvā brahmā hyuvāca tam..
śakrasvabuddhyāvartasva dadhīciṃ gaccha satvaram.. 16.75 ..
1.3.d:
निःस्पृहं तस्य तद्वाक्यं श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मा ह्युवाच तम्..
शक्रस्वबुद्ध्यावर्तस्व दधीचिं गच्छ सत्वरम्.. 16.75 ..
1.3.m: Hearing his detached words, Brahmā said to him: / 'Śakra, act with your own understanding; go quickly to Dadhīci. 16.75

1.3.s:
yācasva tasya cāsthīni dadhīceḥ kāryagauravāt..
guruṇā sahitaḥ śakro devaiḥ saha samanvitaḥ.. 16.76 ..
1.3.d:
याचस्व तस्य चास्थीनि दधीचेः कार्यगौरवात्..
गुरुणा सहितः शक्रो देवैः सह समन्वितः.. 16.76 ..
1.3.m: And beg for his bones from Dadhīci, because of the gravity of this task.' / Accompanied by his Guru and joined together with the gods, Śakra, 16.76

1.3.s:
tatheti gatvā te sarve dadhīcasyāśramaṃ śubham..
nānāsattvasamāyuktaṃ vairabāvavivarjitam.. 16.77 ..
1.3.d:
तथेति गत्वा ते सर्वे दधीचस्याश्रमं शुभम्..
नानासत्त्वसमायुक्तं वैरबावविवर्जितम्.. 16.77 ..
1.3.m: saying, 'So be it,' went, and they all [reached] Dadhīci's auspicious hermitage, / filled with various creatures and free of hostility. 16.77

1.3.s:
mārjāramūṣakāścaiva parasparamudānvitāḥ..
aikapadyena siṃhāśca gajinyaḥ kalabhaiḥ saha.. 16.78 ..
1.3.d:
मार्जारमूषकाश्चैव परस्परमुदान्विताः..
ऐकपद्येन सिंहाश्च गजिन्यः कलभैः सह.. 16.78 ..
1.3.m: Cats and mice were mutually filled with joy; / and lions, in complete harmony, walked alongside female elephants with their calves. 16.78

1.3.s:
tathā jātyaśca vividhāḥ krīḍāyuktāḥ parasparam..
nakulaiḥ saha sarpāśca krīḍāyuktāḥ parasparam.. 16.79 ..
1.3.d:
तथा जात्यश्च विविधाः क्रीडायुक्ताः परस्परम्..
नकुलैः सह सर्पाश्च क्रीडायुक्ताः परस्परम्.. 16.79 ..
1.3.m: Likewise, various species played together; / snakes played with mongooses. 16.79

1.3.s:
evaṃvidhānyanekāni hyaścaryāṇi tadāśrame..
paśyaṃto vibudhāḥ sarve vismayaṃ paramaṃ yayuḥ.. 16.80 ..
1.3.d:
एवंविधान्यनेकानि ह्यश्चर्याणि तदाश्रमे..
पश्यंतो विबुधाः सर्वे विस्मयं परमं ययुः.. 16.80 ..
1.3.m: Seeing many such marvels in that hermitage, / all the gods were filled with the highest astonishment. 16.80

1.3.s:
athāsane muniśreṣṭhaṃ dadṛśuḥ paramāsthitam..
tejasā parameṇaiva bhrājamānaṃ yathā ravim.. 16.81 ..
1.3.d:
अथासने मुनिश्रेष्ठं ददृशुः परमास्थितम्..
तेजसा परमेणैव भ्राजमानं यथा रविम्.. 16.81 ..
1.3.m: Then they saw the best of sages seated on a seat, deeply absorbed [in meditation], / radiant with supreme splendor like the sun, 16.81

1.3.s:
vibhāvasuṃ dvitīyaṃ vā suvarcasahitaṃ tadā..
yathā brahmā hi sāvitryā tathāsau munisattamaḥ.. 16.82 ..
1.3.d:
विभावसुं द्वितीयं वा सुवर्चसहितं तदा..
यथा ब्रह्मा हि सावित्र्या तथासौ मुनिसत्तमः.. 16.82 ..
1.3.m: or like a second fire, accompanied then by Suvarcas, / just as Brahmā [is accompanied] by Sāvitrī, so was this best of sages. 16.82

1.3.s:
taṃ praṇamya tato devā vacanaṃ cedamabruvan..
tvaṃ dātā triṣu lokeṣu tvatsakāśamihagatāḥ.. 16.83 ..
1.3.d:
तं प्रणम्य ततो देवा वचनं चेदमब्रुवन्..
त्वं दाता त्रिषु लोकेषु त्वत्सकाशमिहगताः.. 16.83 ..
1.3.m: Then, having bowed to him, the gods spoke these words: / 'You are a giver throughout the three worlds; we have come here into your presence.' 16.83

1.3.s:
niśamya vacanaṃ teṣāṃ devānāṃ bhunirabravīt..
kimartha māgatāḥ sarve vadadhvaṃ tatsurottamāḥ.. 16.84 ..
1.3.d:
निशम्य वचनं तेषां देवानां भुनिरब्रवीत्..
किमर्थ मागताः सर्वे वदध्वं तत्सुरोत्तमाः.. 16.84 ..
1.3.m: Hearing the words of those gods, the sage said: / 'For what purpose have you all come? Tell it, O best of gods! 16.84

1.3.s:
prayacchāmi na saṃdeho nānyathā mama bhāṣitam..
tadocuḥ sahitāḥ sarve dadhīciṃ svārthakāmukāḥ.. 16.85 ..
1.3.d:
प्रयच्छामि न संदेहो नान्यथा मम भाषितम्..
तदोचुः सहिताः सर्वे दधीचिं स्वार्थकामुकाः.. 16.85 ..
1.3.m: I shall give it, of that there is no doubt; my word is not otherwise.' / Then all of them, desiring their own purpose, together spoke to Dadhīci: 16.85

1.3.s:
bhayabhītā vayaṃ vipra bhavaddarśanakāṃkṣiṇaḥ..
trātāraṃ tvāṃ samākarṇya brahmaṇā noditā vayam.. 16.86 ..
1.3.d:
भयभीता वयं विप्र भवद्दर्शनकांक्षिणः..
त्रातारं त्वां समाकर्ण्य ब्रह्मणा नोदिता वयम्.. 16.86 ..
1.3.m: 'Stricken with fear, O brahmin, we were longing for your darśana; / having heard that you are our protector, we were dispatched by Brahmā. 16.86

1.3.s: samprāptā viddhi tatsarvaṃ dātumarho'tha suvrata.. 16.87 ..
1.3.d: सम्प्राप्ता विद्धि तत्सर्वं दातुमर्होऽथ सुव्रत.. 16.87 ..
1.3.m: Know all that; we have arrived; therefore, O one of noble vows, you ought to grant it.' 16.87

1.3.s: niśamya vacanaṃ teṣāṃ kiṃ dātavyaṃ taducyatām.. 16.88 ..
1.3.d: निशम्य वचनं तेषां किं दातव्यं तदुच्यताम्.. 16.88 ..
1.3.m: Hearing their words, [he said:] 'What is to be given? Let that be said.' 16.88

1.3.s:
tato devābruvanvipra daityānāṃ nidhanāyanaḥ..
śastranirmāṇakāryārthaṃ tavāsthīni prayaccha vai.. 16.89 ..
1.3.d:
ततो देवाब्रुवन्विप्र दैत्यानां निधनायनः..
शस्त्रनिर्माणकार्यार्थं तवास्थीनि प्रयच्छ वै.. 16.89 ..
1.3.m: Then the gods said: 'O brahmin, for our slaughter of the daityas, / for the sake of fashioning weapons, grant your bones!' 16.89

1.3.s:
prahasyovāca viprarṣistiṣṭhadhvaṃ kṣaṇameva hi..
svayameva tvahaṃ devāstyakṣyāmyadya kalevaram.. 16.90 ..
1.3.d:
प्रहस्योवाच विप्रर्षिस्तिष्ठध्वं क्षणमेव हि..
स्वयमेव त्वहं देवास्त्यक्ष्याम्यद्य कलेवरम्.. 16.90 ..
1.3.m: Smiling, the brahmin seer said: 'Wait for just a moment; / I myself, O gods, will cast off this body today.' 16.90

1.3.s:
ityuktvā tānatho patnīṃ samāhūya suvarcasam..
provāca sa mahātejāḥ śrṛṇu devī śucismite.. 16.91 ..
1.3.d:
इत्युक्त्वा तानथो पत्नीं समाहूय सुवर्चसम्..
प्रोवाच स महातेजाः श्रृणु देवी शुचिस्मिते.. 16.91 ..
1.3.m: Having said this to them, then calling his wife Suvarcas, / that sage of great splendor said: 'Listen, O goddess of pure smiles! 16.91

1.3.s:
asthyarthaṃ yācito devaistyajāmyetatkalevaram..
brahmalokaṃ vrajāmyadya parameṇa samādhinā.. 16.92 ..
1.3.d:
अस्थ्यर्थं याचितो देवैस्त्यजाम्येतत्कलेवरम्..
ब्रह्मलोकं व्रजाम्यद्य परमेण समाधिना.. 16.92 ..
1.3.m: Begged by the gods for my bones, I am casting off this body. / Today I go to Brahmaloka through supreme samādhi. 16.92

1.3.s:
mayi yāte brahmalokaṃ tvaṃ svadharmeṇa tatra mām..
prāpsyasyeva na saṃdeho vṛthā cintāṃ ca mā kṛthāḥ.. 16.93 ..
1.3.d:
मयि याते ब्रह्मलोकं त्वं स्वधर्मेण तत्र माम्..
प्राप्स्यस्येव न संदेहो वृथा चिन्तां च मा कृथाः.. 16.93 ..
1.3.m: When I have gone to Brahmaloka, you, by your own duty, will surely / attain me there, no doubt; do not be anxious in vain.' 16.93

1.3.s:
ityuktvā tāṃ svapatnīṃ sa preṣayāmāsa cāśramam..
tato devāgrato vipraḥ samādhimagamattadā.. 16.94 ..
1.3.d:
इत्युक्त्वा तां स्वपत्नीं स प्रेषयामास चाश्रमम्..
ततो देवाग्रतो विप्रः समाधिमगमत्तदा.. 16.94 ..
1.3.m: Having spoken thus to his wife, he sent her away into the hermitage. / Then, in the presence of the gods, the brahmin entered samādhi. 16.94

1.3.s:
samādhinā pareṇaiva visṛjya svaṃ kalevaram..
brahmalokaṃ gataḥ sadyaḥ punarnāvartate yataḥ.. 16.95 ..
1.3.d:
समाधिना परेणैव विसृज्य स्वं कलेवरम्..
ब्रह्मलोकं गतः सद्यः पुनर्नावर्तते यतः.. 16.95 ..
1.3.m: Abandoning his own body through supreme samādhi, / he immediately went to Brahmaloka, from where one does not return. 16.95

1.3.s:
dadhīcināmā munivṛṃdavaryaḥ śivapriyaḥ śivadīkṣābhiyuktaḥ..
paropakārārthamidaṃ kalevaraṃ śīghraṃ sa vipro'tyajadātmanā tadā.. 16.96 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ prathame māheśvarakhaṇḍe kedārakhaṇḍe devairasthikṛtā'bhyarthitasya dadhīceryogena svadehavisarjananāma ṣoḍaśo'dhyāyaḥ.. 16 .. cha ..
1.3.d:
दधीचिनामा मुनिवृंदवर्यः शिवप्रियः शिवदीक्षाभियुक्तः..
परोपकारार्थमिदं कलेवरं शीघ्रं स विप्रोऽत्यजदात्मना तदा.. 16.96 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां प्रथमे माहेश्वरखण्डे केदारखण्डे देवैरस्थिकृताऽभ्यर्थितस्य दधीचेर्योगेन स्वदेहविसर्जननाम षोडशोऽध्यायः.. 16 .. छ ..
1.3.m:
The best among hosts of sages named Dadhīci, beloved of Śiva, committed to Śiva's initiation, / that brahmin then quickly cast off his body of his own accord for the sake of helping others. 16.96
Thus ends the sixteenth chapter, named 'The Relinquishment of His Own Body through Yoga by Dadhīci, Supplicated for His Bones by the Gods,' in the Kedārakhaṇḍa of the first section, the Māheśvarakhaṇḍa, in the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa of eighty-one thousand verses. 16.

1.3.s:
..lomaśa uvāca..
tataḥ sarve suragaṇā dṛṣṭvā taṃ vilayaṃ gatam..
ciṃtayaṃtaḥ suragaṇāḥ kathaṃ ca vidadhāmahe.. 17.1 ..
1.3.d:
..लोमश उवाच..
ततः सर्वे सुरगणा दृष्ट्वा तं विलयं गतम्..
चिंतयंतः सुरगणाः कथं च विदधामहे.. 17.1 ..
